v1_1_round2_rules.rule: every plan is a STAIRWAY: gradual weekly steps, smaller in the first weeks, slightly bigger after the halfway point but not too much, the hardest weeks last (12-week: the last 4 weeks 'brutal'); 'start at a 2 and end at an 11' = perceived effort / overall load level ending a little past usual limits, not set counts
v1_1_round2_rules.applied_in: plan_length_shapes, season_families, every profile (stairway note in aquatic-endurance-track records; engine shape in 06 / 12 v1.1)

v1_1_round2_rules.rule: no deload or maintenance week inside a block: a block that cannot be completed is cancelled -> maintenance phase (length chosen, extendable; at its end: keep maintaining / change plan / start a training block) -> a whole new block. Pre-season = a 4-6-week block at about 60 % of off-season sets with more speed and power + a 1-2-week taper
v1_1_round2_rules.applied_in: season_overrides.pre_season of every competitive profile, season_families, in_season_content, assembly_rules

v1_1_round2_rules.rule: no check-in = no adaptation (the plan follows its planned stairway); the check-in step comes from effort, completion and pain only - the coach rejected sleep / stress / job inputs ('I just need the workouts'); effort 10 = 'the max I could do, but successful', a separate 'failed' option may exist
v1_1_round2_rules.applied_in: no profile uses lifestyle inputs (consistency check C12); v1_1_resolution_flags
v1_1_round2_rules.v1_2: superseded in v1.2: no check-ins (COACH-R3 VOL-02, VOL-04); the end-of-maintenance prompt is replaced by 'the plan ends and the user builds the next' (COACH-R3 PER-01)

v1_1_round2_rules.rule: floor 10 weekly sets per muscle ('I don't think anybody needs less than 10'); small muscles grow by the same idea; caps approved but customizable; most people train 20-30 sets per muscle per week; above 30 only for very advanced (optional 'pro' level). Rear delts 4 / 6 / 8 own sets approved (flag vs the floor)
v1_1_round2_rules.applied_in: muscle_volume_targets, derived.v1_1_audit.muscles_below_floor_10 on every profile, open questions

not understood by the coach: DEFAULT used - alternate the first exercise between the two weekly exposures; a bonus exercise goes on the optional day

heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days; non-axial hinge / leg press / belt squat on the other days; axial = barbell back / front / zercher / overhead / Smith squats, barbell or trap-bar deadlifts and RDLs, good mornings; powerlifters may add a light technique squat or deadlift
v1_1_round2_rules.applied_in: session_rules, injury_library LOW_BACK_LOADING, every injury_prehab copy of it (text replaced), powerlifting_strength.resistance.axial_rule

v1_1_round2_rules.rule: core opens the session light (2 x 2 short of failure); core supersets / monster sets may be added anywhere; field-athlete cap 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block
full-body days use 2-4 exercises PER MUSCLE trained that day (never 1), even if the day gets longer
v1_1_round2_rules.applied_in: session_load_check, weekend_warrior / genpop budgets (05 v1.1 template basis)

v1_1_round2_rules.rule: aerobic sessions per week adjustable up or down by the user; aesthetics 4 incl. a second easy Orange + optional walks

plyo : ballistic share by ground-contact class approved (sprinters 75; volleyball, soccer, football skill 60; basketball, tennis, football big-skill, weekend warriors 50; baseball, softball, hockey, linemen, MMA 40; boxing, karate, kickboxing, wrestling, BJJ, golf 25); each block starts 15 points more ballistic; ballistic list (squat / box / broad / loaded / hex-bar jumps, medball throws) vs plyometric list (pogo / ankle hops, hurdle hops, depth jumps, bounds, squirrel jumps, repeated jumps); stick-the-landing = the receive stage
v1_1_round2_rules.applied_in: ground_contact + power_mix + power_mix_by_phase on every profile (consistency check C1)

v1_1_round2_rules.rule: 'Receive-Create stages' (1 Land, 2 Land & Go, 3 Repeat); 12-week plan wk 1-3 / 4-7 / 8-12; 8-week 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8; restart at stage 1 each off-season; stay put in maintenance; L2-L3 may start at stage 2
Olympic lifts up to 4x / week (clean days = more squat-pattern, snatch days = more hinge-pattern); in season a light piece; full squat cleans / snatches 3-5 reps with the coach's eye on speed
v1_1_round2_rules.applied_in: olympic_by_level, olympic_policy on every athletic profile

v1_1_round2_rules.rule: aerobic sessions: off-season baseball, softball, sprinters 2; basketball, volleyball, football, tennis, golf, boxing, BJJ 3; soccer, hockey, kickboxing, karate 3-4; MMA, wrestling 4; pre-season 2; powerlifters 2 easy Orange

in season, game-heavy sports (basketball, volleyball, soccer, football, hockey): gym plyos about half, no extra change-of-direction work, sprints only for speed athletes, the one hard gym day at least 48 h before a game

the year plan is gen-pop "stay in shape" planning, fully user-tunable (re-order blocks, more / less cardio, e.g. a winter powerlifting-style block); athletes follow their season
test before the block (or week 1) and at the end, never mid-block; people starting from zero never test a 1RM or a max mile - 5RM / 3RM or 80-90 % efforts
competitive athletes give the season start date (or in season until / competition date) + practice and game days; recreational = activity only, no position or season
weight guidance by RIR / RPE; Olympic lifts explained as power output, % only for competitive Olympic lifters (own programming); neutral Latin American Spanish with English gym terms in brackets
the '21.6 mile run' is removed from plans and tests; the longest run stays the half-marathon plan

v1_1_resolution_flags.topic: Lifestyle inputs removed (R2-GEN-04 vs the approved R2-VOL-01 table)
v1_1_resolution_flags.resolution: The coach approved the R2-VOL-01 check-in step table (which had a 'life was harder' column) but then rejected every lifestyle input (R2-GEN-04: 'I just need the workouts ... no need to talk about sleep or stress or anything else'). Resolution applied in v1.1: no profile, intake field or check-in uses sleep, stress, life or a physical job; the weekly step is decided from effort, completion and pain only (the approved table minus its life column). Sport load (pool yardage, mileage) is not asked either (aquatic-endurance-track.json O5). [v1.2: the check-in itself is RETIRED - COACH-R3 VOL-02, VOL-04]
v1_1_resolution_flags.status_v1_2: RETIRED in v1.2: there are no check-ins at all (COACH-R3 VOL-02, VOL-04); no lifestyle inputs anywhere (COACH-R2 GEN-04)

v1_1_resolution_flags.topic: Rear-delt own sets (4 / 6 / 8, approved R2-VOL-04) vs the floor of 10 (R2-VOL-06)
v1_1_resolution_flags.resolution: Both statements are his: v1.1 keeps the 4 / 6 / 8 own rear-delt sets and counts the 0.25 credit from rows on top; rear delts usually sit below 10 in the audit. PROPOSED reading: rear-delt own sets are 'shoulder health' work and the floor applies to the muscles a plan trains for size - needs the coach's yes.
v1_1_resolution_flags.status_v1_2: CLOSED by COACH-R3 VOL-01: rear delts are part of the shoulders group (front + side + rear); the floor of 10 counts on the group; users / coaches can add rear-delt work (derived.v1_2_group_audit)

v1_1_resolution_flags.topic: Floor of 10 sets per muscle vs athlete budgets
v1_1_resolution_flags.resolution: derived.v1_1_audit lists muscles below 10 for every profile. Most athlete budgets (04 v1 coach programs) leave chest, side delts and arms below 10. PROPOSED reading (team O1, aquatic O1, combat Q1, genpop GP-2): the floor applies to muscles the athlete's plan trains for size / strength in the off-season; pre-season (~60 %) and in-season blocks are maintenance-like. The volume engine (12 v1.1) raises the targets; the profiles stay descriptive budgets.
v1_1_resolution_flags.status_v1_2: PARTLY ANSWERED: COACH-R3 VOL-01 (floor counted on groups, training blocks) and R3-SES-01 / SES-02 (groups trained that day; time-short plans train fewer groups directly, the rest from compound credit); athlete group floors are set by 12 v1.2

v1_1_resolution_flags.resolution: DEFAULT used: alternate the first exercise between the two weekly exposures of a day type; a bonus small-muscle exercise (2 sets) goes on the optional day as a Focus slot (with no optional day, at the end of the shortest training day). Marked DEFAULT - not coach-approved.
v1_1_resolution_flags.status_v1_2: CLOSED: COACH-R3 VOL-03 approved the placement (alternate the first exercise between the two exposures; small-muscle bonus exercise on the optional day or on a day that already trains it, never as its only exercise)

KB swings stay as a ballistic / triple-extension option (e.g. the Olympic substitute for older or injured clients) and credit no muscle (R2-VOL-05).

v1_1_resolution_flags.topic: 60+ default: landing drills yes, low ankle hops opt-in
v1_1_resolution_flags.resolution: The approved R2-ATH-08 proposal kept landing drills and low ankle hops for 60+; the coach's added words say no plyos by default, and 'pogo and ankle hops' are on his own approved plyometric list (R2-ATH-02). v1.1 sport verification: landing drills (RC1 'Land' = step-down and stick, no rebound - the receive stage, not a plyometric) stay as the default floor together with balance, reactive stepping, light throws and fast-concentric machine work; low ankle hops move to the opt-in as its first item (with the warning; useful for bone). This also matches the competitive senior pickleball variant (none by default). Olympic lifts, other plyos and depth jumps stay opt-in only.
v1_1_resolution_flags.status_v1_2: APPROVED: COACH-R3 ATH-02 (landing drills, balance, quick stepping, light throws, fast machine work on; ankle hops, jumps, Olympic lifts and depth jumps off and switchable with the warning)

v1_1_resolution_flags.resolution: swimming_sprint / middle / distance and lap_swim moved from class 4 (40 %) to class 5 (25 %): starts and turns are single big efforts with a long contact = ballistic in the coach's definition (COACH-R2 ATH-02); weekly PLYO / JLK / BALL / THROW re-split at the same total; a small ankle block stays for bone (AQ8).

stay_athletic_standard.title: What a 'stay athletic and active' (athletic but not competitive) plan contains, in the coach's terms
coach_words: COACH-ANSWER ATH-13: a program 'for weekend warriors: people that wanted to be athletic, but they didn't need to compete in any sport ... non-competitive, all-around athletic adults. Youth can be there too, and kids ... a good mix of everything ... good health all around and just having a body that performs well.'

Coach request 2026-10-08 (relayed in this workflow): gen-pop and general-fitness people want 'things like high rows [HYROX] and pickleball, meaning they want to stay athletic and active, so we need to understand that that's an option for them.'
COACH-ANSWER ATH-10: 'everyone gets Olympic lifts' in athletic training (beginners: DB / KB snatches, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls / cleans).

COACH-R2 ATH-08: older adults - no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default, 'an additional option if they want to do it', with 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means.'
stay_athletic_standard.definition: The coach's own non-competitive athletic program (BYOP 'ATHLETIC - FULL BODY - 4 DAYS A', the former 'Justice League' tab, renamed 'Athletic Performance - Non-Competitive') is the template: every main day opens with light core, then a short athletic block (jumps, a throw, a change-of-direction drill, an Olympic lift), then full-body resistance in hip + push / knee + pull pairs, calves and rear delts; optional days carry Focus work and aerobic sessions. Recreational = no position, no season dates, no pre- / in-season blocks (GEN-02); the activity only changes WHICH athletic qualities lead and how much.

per_main_day.dose: 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility; never counted as volume
2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure; movable; core supersets / monster sets may be added anywhere

1-2 jump stations x 2 sets; plyometric vs ballistic by the activity's ground-contact class (75 / 60 / 50 / 40 / 25 %), each block 15 points more ballistic at the start; Receive-Create stages 1 Land -> 2 Land & Go -> 3 Repeat
0-1 medball station x 2 sets (more for rotational activities: racket sports, golf); ball <= 20 lb, lighter for youth and older

0-1 change-of-direction station x 2 sets, EASY -> MOD. TURN (HARD TURN and reactive agility for L2+); none needed for linear / grounded activities, but one light footwork station a week keeps 'some agility' (PROPOSED)

1 station x 2 sets on most main days (up to 4 a week): clean variants on squat days, snatch variants on hinge days; L1 = hang clean, KB squat clean, single-arm DB snatch, hex-bar jump, hang pulls; explained as power output, loaded by RIR / RPE
per_main_day.tag: COACH-ANSWER ATH-10; COACH-R2 ATH-04/05, GEN-06, LIB-07

per_main_day.dose: 2-4 exercises per muscle group trained that day (never 1); hip-dominant + push, knee-dominant + pull; cross-pattern pairing; heavy squat and heavy deadlift on different days; volume by the engine: general factor x0.8, floor 10 sets a week per trained group (hips, shoulders ... - COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01), stairway steps
per_main_day.tag: COACH-ANSWER UNI-06, UNI-11; COACH-R2 SES-01/02/05, VOL-04/06, PER-03/04; COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01; 12 v1.2 §3.4

per_main_day.dose: calves: one exercise x 3 sets every leg day (COACH-R3 SES-01); rear delts / KB face pulls inside the shoulders group (front + side + rear delts; the floor of 10 counts on the group; users / coaches can add more rear-delt work - COACH-R3 VOL-01)
3 sessions a week - one Blue (A), one Green (B), one Orange (C); the user can add or remove sessions; a 45-60+ min session of the activity counts as one of the 3 (up to 2) (COACH-R3 ATH-05)
per_main_day.tag: COACH-ANSWER ATH-07, EQ-14; COACH-R2 SES-06; COACH-R3 ATH-05

how_much_by_days.2_days: 2 main days + the activity: ~4 athletic stations a day (8-10 sets), resistance on the 05 2-day template; aerobic = the activity + 0-1 gym sessions
how_much_by_days.3_days: the default for most activities: 4-5 athletic stations a day (10-14 sets per day at most, often less), resistance on the 05 3-day template (S1 squat / S2 non-axial hinge / S3 deadlift)
how_much_by_days.4_days: the coach's own template (weekend warrior): 2 jumps + 1 throw + 1 COD + 1 Olympic a day (about 10 athletic sets a day), 2 optional days
how_much_by_days.evidence: OBSERVED BYOP athletic slots (OT04) + 05 v1.1 templates; scaling PROPOSED

weekly_ranges.fast_reactive_plyometric_contacts: 0-56 (gen-pop sits below the coach's field-athlete bands; 60+ default 0 - low ankle hops are opt-in)
weekly_ranges.throws: 0-80 (rotational activities and the weekend warrior at the top)
weekly_ranges.cod_cuts: 0-56 (court activities and the weekend warrior at the top)
weekly_ranges.evidence: computed from the 18 profiles in this file (derived.nominal_weekly_dose_from_sets); PROPOSED

share_of_weekly_sets_in_these_profiles.note: The coach's own weekend-warrior template was about 32 % athletic sets in 04 v1 (40 of 124); with the v1.1 resistance block (R2-SES-05, 2-4 exercises per muscle group) it is about 25 %; endurance and 60+ profiles sit lower, court and youth profiles higher (computed)

dial.scale: 0 none - 1 a little - 2 regular - 3 leads the plan (analyst summary, PROPOSED)

what_it_is_not: not competitive: no position, no season start date, no pre-season or in-season blocks (COACH-ANSWER GEN-02)
no contrast / French-contrast complexes by default - they are for L2+ athletes in an off-season (COACH-ANSWER ATH-12; gen-pop reading INFERRED)
not aesthetics: medball throws stay in the main workout (ATH-05 removes them only for aesthetics)
no 1RM or max-mile tests from zero (COACH-R2 PER-07)
no lifestyle questions (sleep, stress, job) - workouts only (COACH-R2 GEN-04)
stay_athletic_standard.play_days: the user can enter the days they play: the hardest gym day stays at least 48 h before the biggest play day; weeks with 3+ play sessions drop the extra agility drills and half the jumps; a 45-60+ minute session of the activity counts as one of the 3 cardio sessions (up to 2) (COACH-R3 ATH-05, approved)
stay_athletic_standard.event_date: optional (a first HYROX race, a pickleball tournament, a 10K): the hardest weeks end 1 week before, then 1 easy week at about half the sets; after the event the plan ends and the user builds the next one (COACH-R3 ATH-05, PER-01)
stay_athletic_standard.year: the gen-pop year stays the default and is fully user-tunable (re-order blocks, more / less cardio, e.g. a winter strength block); an activity block can be dropped where the user wants it (COACH-R2 PER-01/02)
stay_athletic_standard.no_check_in: RETIRED check-ins (COACH-R3 VOL-02, VOL-04): the plan is printed once with its built-in stairway; people and coaches adjust it themselves; nothing is stored (COACH-R3 GEN-01)
stay_athletic_standard.older_60_plus: COACH-R3 ATH-02 (approved): from 60 the defaults ON are landing drills (step down and stick, no bounce), balance, quick stepping without a hop, light medball throws and fast machine work; low ankle hops, other jumps, Olympic lifts and depth jumps are OFF and can be switched on with the warning 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means'; overhead squats and low-bar squats stay out (snatch variants stay out too - COACH-ANSWER EQ-03, not revisited); W_OLDER_POWER: 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means.'
stay_athletic_standard.youth: kids and teens can use it (ATH-13); floor Olympic lifts from about 14 after a hang block (COACH-R2 ATH-08); youth_general_athletic profile
stay_athletic_standard.evidence: COACH (ATH-13, ATH-10, ATH-11, ATH-07, R2-ATH-01/03/04/08, R2-SES-03/05, R2-VOL-04/06) for the parts; doses per activity PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL; round 3: COACH-R3 ATH-02 / ATH-03 / ATH-04 / ATH-05 / SES-02 approved the play-day, cardio-credit, event-date, older, racket and HYROX parts
stay_athletic_standard.racket_50_plus: COACH-R3 ATH-02 (approved): pickleball, padel and tennis players 50+ get knee-friendly strength, calf and Achilles work every leg day, rotator-cuff work, and only low-impact jumps (no depth jumps, hurdle hops or bounds) unless switched on
stay_athletic_standard.hyrox_plan: COACH-R3 ATH-03 (approved HYROX plan): 2 strength days (squat + pull, deadlift + push) + 2 hybrid days (run intervals, or 1 km run + 1 station repeated); 4 cardio sessions (Blue, Green, Orange + a second Orange) because running is about half the race; 2 short station circuits a week (sled push / pull, burpee broad jumps, wall balls, farmers carry, sandbag lunges, SkiErg / row) as finishers that do not count as muscle sets; wall balls with the race ball (never over 20 lb); 40-rep / AMRAP sets only inside these circuits; jumps 50 % plyometric, like basketball
stay_athletic_standard.editing_r3: the user or coach can switch off a day's athletic block or core block (e.g. a pickleball player with sore calves), add or remove exercises or whole blocks, and the plan recommends supersets to save time (COACH-R3 SES-02)

New per-profile attribute `ground_contact` (class 1-5) and a derived plyo : ballistic split of power sets (PROPOSED map 75/60/50/40/25 % plyo, floor 20, ceiling 80); new BALL category (ballistic jumps) split out of PLYO; programs start ballistic and become more plyometric.
The coach's written athletic work was re-classified by ground contact (v1_power_mix.py): BASEBALL blocks 36-44% plyo, BOXER weeks 3-6 30%, MM athletic 8-33% - these anchor the class map.

Confirmed plyo ranking is now enforced by construction on a new PLYOMETRIC-contacts dial (fast-SSC, high amplitude): basketball = volleyball > sprinters > football skill > soccer > MMA > tennis > baseball > hockey > wrestling / BJJ > boxing = karate > golf. The v0 scale (all jump contacts) is kept as the NSCA safety check. Resolves v0 open questions 1-3.
Resistance vs speed/power groups encoded per profile (`ath03_group`); rugby mapped to lineman / big-skill profiles, heavyweight fighters by body weight, track & field throwers added as a variant.

Bilateral : unilateral share per profile on the 90/10 <-> 10/90 scale with block-start, block-end and in-season values (bodybuilders / powerlifters 50/50 -> 80/20-90/10; field / COD athletes 80-90% unilateral; in-season bilateral minimal); upper body follows the same logic; weekly set budgets re-split to the mid-block value.

Contralateral (into the hip: COD sports - football, soccer, basketball, tennis) vs ipsilateral (out of the hip: sprint acceleration, ipsilateral step-ups); contra/ipsi as health accessories for bodybuilders / powerlifters mostly in weeks 1-4.
Frontal / transverse share of unilateral lower sets per profile (high for basketball, tennis, soccer, MMA and other court / combat athletes; low for aesthetics).

Pairing: same-pattern for aesthetics and high-level athletes, cross-pattern for bootcamp / general; hip-dominant + push and knee-dominant + pull in full-body and bootcamp days (Bootcamp Option 1 Tue/Fri wiring corrected).

Boxers (and, by extension, strikers) REDUCE pressing, vertical pulling and arm isolation when punching volume is high - never cut to zero; SHOULDER_STRIKER rule and boxing budget changed (HPUSH 3, VPULL 3, arms 2 + 2).

Medball volume by sport: high for baseball, boxing, MMA, tennis, golf; moderate for basketball and football; none in the main workout for aesthetics (warm-up only); ball never over 20 lb; no band chops; a throwing slot can be the whole ~19-throw list.
Aerobic sessions/week: 3 general and fat loss, 2 athletes in season, 4 aesthetics / bodybuilders + long walks after workouts; fighters get a real aerobic block; athlete off-season counts PROPOSED.
Pitcher variant confirmed: less overhead pressing, more arm care, rotational throws kept light.

No sex-based logic anywhere (female-athlete landing rule, softball rationale and bone-stress list removed; v0 open question 14 answered): age, foundation, goal and injuries decide. Older clients: few plyos unless asked. Youth: some Olympic lifts from the floor.

Everyone in athletic training gets Olympic lifts by level (L1 DB/KB snatch, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls/cleans; L2+ full 'Squat' lifts); Olympic dose raised where it was optional or zero (baseball 0.6 -> 8, golf, soccer, tennis, karate, BJJ, youth, distance runner).
Contrast / complexes: L2+ athletes, off-season only, ~78-85%, no rest inside the complex.

The 'Justice League' name is retired: the profile is now 'All-around athletic / weekend warrior (non-competitive adults and youth)' (`weekend_warrior`, was `athlete_generic`); the sheet tab is cited only as a source.
In-season content by athlete type: speed athletes -> sprints, most others -> strength maintenance, some -> high jumps; about 2 lifting days; minimal bilateral; 2 aerobic sessions.
High school, college and pro baseball (and other) athletes share the same plan; loads and speeds differ; pros get more care. Competition level is a modifier, not a profile. Thursday = strength.

Older, injured and high-volume clients collect volume on constrained machines (compounds and isolation); never overhead squat, snatch, low-bar squat, depth jumps; new HIGH_VOLUME_CONSTRAINT rule; hack squat no longer 'deprioritised' (machines are not ranked).
No bands or variable resistance in any generator rule (banded neck, banded adduction, chained / banded pulls, 'reverse banded' squirrel jumps written unbanded).
Muscle credit map: helpers 0.25 (was 0.5); unilateral knee-dominant credits quads 1.0, glutes 0.25; athletic sets credit no muscle. Per-muscle table recomputed.
Calves 3 sets every leg day, rear delts their own sets, about 2 core exercises for athletes; core FIRST in every session (movable). Weekly budgets updated.
Session caps and length per population added to the assembly rules (field athletes off-season up to 10-12 exercises; resistance-only 5-7; ~1.5 h athletes, 45-60 min general).

Plan-length shapes rewritten: 4-6-week maintenance / transition at 50-70% volume, 8-week = 4 adapt + 4 drive, 12-week = 2-4 acclimation + 4-6 build + hardest last weeks, repeated cycles one level higher, week-by-week and yearly modes; deload ~half the sets; tests by checkbox; VOL 1/2/3 per block for all athletes.

headline_findings: COACH-ANSWER ATH-01 / CAT-10: what decides plyos vs ballistics is how long the sport keeps the athlete on the ground - short contacts (sprinters) -> more plyos, long contacts (karate, fighters, baseball) -> more ballistics, basketball 'a good mix'; programs start ballistic and become plyometric. v1 encodes a `ground_contact` class (1-5) per sport and derives the plyo share of power sets (PROPOSED map 75 / 60 / 50 / 40 / 25%, floor 20, ceiling 80). OBSERVED anchors from a re-count of his own programs by ground contact: BASEBALL blocks 44% / 36% / 44% plyo side, BOXER weeks 3-6 30%, MM athletic STARTING / MID / ADVANCED 33% / 8% / 9% (throw-dominant).

COACH-ANSWER ATH-02 (ranking confirmed): basketball = volleyball > sprinters > football skill > soccer > MMA > tennis > baseball > hockey > wrestling / BJJ > boxing = karate > golf. v1 applies it to FAST-reactive plyometric contacts (the ground-contact definition): the boxer's 113-129 weekly jump contacts are mostly ballistic jumps (66) and landings (24), only 31 are fast-reactive, below baseball's 37 / 58 / 74 - so the coach's own programs agree with his ranking once contacts are classified his way. Targets follow the ranking by construction (section 5.12).

COACH-ANSWER UNI-02 / UNI-03 / UNI-10: bilateral : unilateral runs from 90/10 to 10/90 by athlete, goal, phase and pain - bodybuilders / powerlifters about 50/50 at the start then 80/20-90/10 bilateral, field / change-of-direction athletes 80-90% unilateral, bilateral minimal in season; unilateral = health and rotational foundation, bilateral = driving force; upper body the same. OBSERVED today: 26-32% unilateral in strength / conjugate, ~50% in the BYOP 4-day templates, 43-47% in baseball (every block, including in-season), 50-75% in the MM athletic blocks, 63% HYBRID. v1 sets block-start / block-end / in-season values per profile (section 5.11).

COACH-ANSWER CAT-13 / UNI-12 / UNI-06: contralateral loading pulls you INTO the hip (change-of-direction athletes: football, soccer, basketball, tennis), ipsilateral helps you OUT of the hip (sprint acceleration - ipsilateral step-ups); for bodybuilders / powerlifters contra/ipsi work is a health accessory mostly in weeks 1-4. Court and combat athletes get more frontal / transverse unilateral work, aesthetics clients little. Same-pattern pairing (squat + lunge) drives a muscle harder (aesthetics, high-level athletes); cross-pattern pairing keeps bootcamp clients less sore.

COACH-ANSWER ATH-05 / EQ-06: medball volume is high for baseball, boxing, MMA, tennis and golf, moderate for basketball and football, and NONE in the main workout for aesthetics clients (warm-up only); balls never over 20 lb. OBSERVED volumes: 176-192 throws/week in baseball (block means; single weeks 70-290; 45-63% transverse), 190 -> 380 for the boxer, 210 -> 400 -> 420 in the MM athletic blocks (210 and 420 ASSUMED from 'ALL LIST'), 64-96 in the BYOP athletic template at 2 sets.

COACH-ANSWER ATH-10 / ATH-12 / ATH-09: everyone in athletic training gets Olympic lifts (L1: DB/KB snatches, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls / cleans without bumpers; L2+: full 'Squat' lifts), youth may do some from the floor; contrast / complexes only for L2+ athletes in the off-season at ~78-85%. v1 raises the Olympic dose where it was optional or zero (baseball 0.6 -> 8 sets, golf, soccer, tennis, karate, BJJ, youth, distance runners).

COACH-ANSWER ATH-07 / ORD-09: aerobic sessions per week = 3 for general and fat-loss clients, 2 for athletes in season, 4 for aesthetics / bodybuilders plus long walks after workouts; fighters get a real aerobic block, not a warm-up. OBSERVED today: physique colour C 2x/week; fat loss C 2x + 2 metabolic circuits (12 -> 33 min work); boxer one A + one C; baseball only short A-type buy-outs (10-39 s, 3-4 bouts/week); HYBRID one A + one C; CrossFit 2-4 by level + 1-4 WODs.

COACH-ANSWER ATH-04: boxers REDUCE pressing and arm volume when punching volume is high - 'don't completely cut it'. OBSERVED: the boxing tab removed horizontal push, vertical pull and arm isolation in weeks 3-8; v1 keeps HPUSH 3, VPULL 3 and 2 + 2 arm sets in the boxing budget and applies the same reduce-not-cut rule to the other strikers.

COACH-ANSWER PER-08: in season, speed athletes sprint, most others maintain strength, some keep high jumps; about 2 lifting days, low volume, bilateral minimal, 2 aerobic sessions; pre-season = more speed / power, less volume (PER-08 RIGHT) - the v1 season multipliers (section 7) follow this, not the observed baseball volumes. OBSERVED (BASEBALL; season labels INFERRED from dates): off-season = new menu every week, '12/10/8/8', OLY late; pre-season = +47% jump contacts, x3 sprint sets, contrast complexes, OLY 75 -> 90%, resistance flat then +2.6 / +3.8 / +3.7% per week, DELOAD (-31% resistance, -46% all sets); in-season = flat 4 x 10, no compound below 8 reps, no Olympic lifts, two alternating proven menus.

COACH-ANSWER ATH-09 / GEN-02: no rule depends on sex - age, foundation (training experience), goal and injuries decide. v1 removed the female-athlete landing rule, the softball 'female populations' rationale and the sex-based bone-stress list. Older clients get few plyos unless they ask; older, injured and high-volume clients collect volume on constrained machines and never get the overhead squat, snatch, low-bar squat or depth jumps (EQ-03).

COACH-ANSWER PRG-09: high school, college and pro athletes need the same things; loads and speeds change, pros get more care (contracts), college athletes adapt as much as they can, high school athletes 'just have to do a lot of work'. Competition level is therefore a modifier on loads and progression, not a separate profile.

COACH-ANSWER ATH-13: the 'Justice League' tab was a marketing name for a weekend-warrior program (non-competitive athletic adults and youth). The profile is now 'All-around athletic / weekend warrior' (`weekend_warrior`), and it is also where recreational players of any sport land (GEN-02).

OBSERVED athletic share of weekly working sets (excluding medball throws): 0% in every physique, bootcamp and fat-loss template and - after COACH-ANSWER ORD-08 (A-drills are warm-up) - 0% in the gym UPPER/LOWER and PPL examples too; 5% strength/conjugate (one 3x6 'EASY' plyo); 16% HYBRID; 16-22% BASEBALL; 32% BYOP athletic at the coach's 2-sets dose; 28% -> 19% -> 15% across the MM athletic STARTING / MID / ADVANCED blocks; 36% for the boxer's conversion weeks.

OBSERVED + INFERRED: the BYOP templates share one resistance skeleton (knee + pull / hip + push, bilateral -> unilateral -> isolation, every pattern 2x/week - pairing confirmed by UNI-11 / ORD-06) and swap the PREFIX: athletic slots for athletes, calves / biceps / triceps for physique, cardio slots for bootcamp. BASEBALL (Parts A-E) and BOXING (3x10 base -> complexes) are structurally different programs that reuse the same 8-pattern vocabulary, so 'one skeleton, many dials' is an INFERRED modelling choice.

COACH-ANSWER VOL-09 / VOL-10 / UNI-01 / VOL-17: helpers get 0.25 set (not 0.5), a 10/10 unilateral set is 1 set credited mainly to the primary muscle, athletic sets never count toward muscles, calves get 3 sets every leg day, rear delts their own sets and athletes about 2 core exercises a session. The per-muscle table (5.6) is recomputed with the 0.25 map; weekly budgets now carry the calves / rear-delt / core sets the coach says he always had athletes do but never wrote.

COACH-ANSWER ATH-11: core goes FIRST, as the warm-up, for everybody (movable after the plyos or the strength block if the user prefers) - replacing the v0 reading (BYOP core on optional days; BASEBALL core second; MM STARTING first / second / last). OBSERVED core-by-plane: BASEBALL rotates 'LATERAL CORE' (Mon), 'Transverse core' (Tue/Fri), 'Sagital core' (Thu) -> 48% transverse, 24% sagittal, 22% frontal sets.

COACH-ANSWER ATH-06 / LIB-21: the route-tree COD names are for every athlete, tiered by turn angle, and MACH drills plus the fixed speed-session order go into the library. OBSERVED: change of direction is zero in every MASTER_MODEL program; only the BYOP athletic template has COD (4 slots/week = 48-64 cuts at 2 sets); sprinting has no BYOP slot.

OBSERVED: 'level' moved volume in opposite directions by population - athletes STARTING -> MID -> ADVANCED: working sets -19% and -18%, jump contacts -51% and -55%, throws +90% and +5%; gym clients NOVICE -> NEWBY -> INTERMEDIATE: weekly sets +18-23% and +13-14%. COACH-ANSWER PRG-04 says STARTING / MID / ADVANCED are blocks or levels 'depending on whatever is needed', PRG-05 defines L1-L3 by training experience in years, and PRG-06 asks for one sound rep/set algorithm for every model (the upper-day rep rise was a fill error).

OBSERVED combat phasing (boxer): 2-week hypertrophy base (3 x 10 on all 8 patterns, no plyos) -> 6-week conversion (exercise list replaced, contrast complexes of the 'ALL ABOUT SQUATS' 'FRENCH CONTRAST' type - the boxing tab never uses that term, 2-week steps, wk 7 accessory mini-deload while the hinge complex / clean & press / row superset rise 3 -> 4 -> 6 sets, wk 8 peak). Steps and waves for fight prep are confirmed (PER-10).

OBSERVED injury logic the coach already uses (and confirmed by VOL-03 / UNI-08 / EQ-03): joint pain -> unilateral and split grips (DB/KB) first, cut the pattern 30-50%, machines, or drop the exercise; throwers press mostly with DBs / landmine / single-arm (barbell overhead pressing appears 3 times in the baseball year); Copenhagen planks appear in the athletic, boxing and baseball programs. SCIENCE adds Nordics (-51% hamstring injuries), Copenhagen (-41% groin problems), landing-first neuromuscular training (about -50% non-contact ACL injuries), jumper's-knee volume caps (44.6% prevalence in volleyball, 31.9% in basketball).

MATRIX v1: 27 profiles and 24 position/phase variants, each a weekly set budget per category (PLYO, JLK, BALL, THROW, COD, SPRINT, TE, 8 resistance patterns, isolations, CORE, FOCUS) so shares, muscle sets, plyo:ballistic split and contact checks are computed, not asserted. Off-season main days land at 16.3-44 sets and an estimated 41-80 minutes (PROPOSED time heuristic), inside the coach's 1.5 h (max 2 h) athlete cap; the general-population profile sits at about 43 min against the 45-60 min general cap, fat loss at about 62 min, just over it (UNI-09). v1 verification: by EXERCISE COUNT most athlete profiles exceed the coach's 10-12 cap (VOL-08) when each category gets its own exercises - session_load_check adds the check and a PROPOSED consolidation rule.

3.label: mixed
3.typical: short jumps and cuts mixed with planted, longer pushes (over 0.25 s = slow SSC [S32])
3.examples: basketball ('good mix'), tennis, football big-skill, youth, weekend warriors

4.typical: planted rotational or pushing actions, well over 0.25 s on the ground (stride-plant-rotate, skating push, stance blocks)

ground_contact_model.evidence: COACH-ANSWER ATH-01 / CAT-10 (rule); class shares APPROVED per sport in COACH-R2 ATH-01 (sprinters 75; volleyball, soccer, football skill 60; basketball, tennis, football big-skill, weekend warriors 50; baseball, softball, hockey, linemen, MMA 40; boxing, karate, kickboxing, wrestling, BJJ, golf 25); the remaining sports approved in COACH-R3 ATH-04 (approved_v1_2); classes of sports on neither list stay INFERRED / PROPOSED
ground_contact_model.science: fast stretch-shortening cycle = ground contact under about 250 ms, slow SSC = over about 250 ms (Schmidtbleicher's split, used by Flanagan & Comyns 2008 to prescribe plyometrics by contact time and reactive strength index [S32]); sprint contacts average about 0.14-0.16 s in acceleration and shorten toward maximal velocity, and faster accelerators show shorter contacts [S33]

bilateral_unilateral_model.scale: share of lower-body compound sets that are BILATERAL : UNILATERAL, anywhere from 90/10 to 10/90 (COACH-ANSWER UNI-02); upper body follows the same logic for pressing and pulling (UNI-03); coach-adjustable
bilateral_unilateral_model.why: 'the unilateral work is more for health and keeping rotational foundations, and the bilateral is more for driving and creating forces' (UNI-02)
anchors: bodybuilders / powerlifters: about 50/50 at the start (unilateral as a small health foundation), then 80/20 -> 90/10 bilateral (COACH-ANSWER UNI-02)
field / change-of-direction athletes (tennis example): 80-90% unilateral in the gym; bilateral = health foundation for connective tissue and joints (COACH-ANSWER UNI-02)
in-season athletes: bilateral kept minimal (maintain strength and potentiation), unilateral keeps ranges of motion and health (COACH-ANSWER UNI-10)
pain or injury moves the share (usually toward unilateral / split grips, or to machines) - COACH-ANSWER UNI-02, VOL-03, MASTER_MODEL athletic A6
bilateral_unilateral_model.engine: share(week) = start + (end - start) x week_fraction across the off-season block (the coach's set-addition order adds sets to the FIRST exercise first, VOL-07, and bilateral slots come first, so the bilateral share rises naturally for size/strength goals); in-season value replaces it during the season; pain overrides; the weekly-set baseline in section 5.2 uses the mid-block value (PROPOSED). For profiles whose share moves TOWARD unilateral (field / COD athletes, e.g. basketball 20/80 -> 10/90), the share target decides where an added set goes: when adding it to the first (bilateral) exercise would move the share away from the week's target, it goes to the first unilateral exercise instead (PROPOSED - reconciles VOL-07 with UNI-02).

contra_ipsi.contralateral: load in the hand opposite the working leg pulls you INTO the hip (eccentric coil); used for change-of-direction athletes who must get in and out of the hip quickly and need the range (football route runners, soccer, basketball 'a lot', tennis 'definitely') - COACH-ANSWER CAT-13
contra_ipsi.ipsilateral: load on the same side helps you OUT of the hip; used for sprint acceleration (e.g. ipsilateral step-ups for a 100 m sprinter's take-off) - COACH-ANSWER CAT-13
contra_ipsi.size_strength: bodybuilders / powerlifters: contra/ipsi lunges and step-ups are HEALTH accessories (hips, low back, the rotational forces lost in symmetrical lifting), mostly in the first 2-4 weeks of a program, then mostly bilateral; kept as an accessory later only if something bugs them - COACH-ANSWER CAT-13
contra_ipsi.pairing: same-pattern pairing (squat + lunge) drives one muscle harder for aesthetics and high-level athletes who need more stimulus; cross-pattern pairing (squat + single-leg RDL) for bootcamp / general clients so they are less sore and can train more often - COACH-ANSWER UNI-06

assembly_rules: 1. Intake (COACH-ANSWER GEN-02, COACH-R2 GEN-05): goal; competitive sport -> sport + position + season start date + practice / game days, recreational -> activity only (activities[]); no sleep / stress / job inputs (COACH-R2 GEN-04); training experience in YEARS (-> L1 / L2 / L3, PRG-05); age; body weight; days; session length; equipment; injuries / pain; Focus muscle 1 / 2 (optional, max 2 - COACH-R3 SES-01); rep-style preference; plan type. NO sex field (GEN-02, ATH-09).

2. Pick the profile from sports[] / activities[] (position -> profile, + variant), season phase and competition level (high school / college / pro = same plan, different loads - PRG-09). A competitive sport without a profile uses the nearest profile by ground-contact class and ATH-03 group (PROPOSED).

3. Weekly set budget per category = profile.weekly_sets (v1 off-season build baseline) x season multiplier x the volume engine's planned stairway step (approved COACH-R3 VOL-04; no check-ins - COACH-R3 VOL-02). Plan type shapes the curve: every plan is a stairway, hardest weeks last (COACH-R2 PER-03 / PER-04); maintenance at 50-70 % volume, length chosen, only as a recommendation after a block (COACH-R2 PER-06; COACH-R3 PER-01).

4. Power block: split power sets plyo : ballistic by the ground-contact class (ATH-01; map PROPOSED), start ballistic-biased and move to the target (CAT-10); plyo method stage 1 -> 2 -> 3 across the block; unilateral plyos after bilateral; medball volume by sport, none for aesthetics, ball <= 20 lb (ATH-05 / EQ-06); Olympic lifts for every athletic trainee at their level (ATH-10); contrast only L2+ off-season (ATH-12).

5. Resistance block: bilateral : unilateral share from the profile (block start -> end, in-season value; UNI-02 / UNI-10), the same logic for upper-body pressing and pulling (UNI-03); contralateral for COD athletes, ipsilateral for acceleration, contra/ipsi as early-block health accessories for size/strength clients (CAT-13); frontal / transverse unilateral share for court and combat athletes (UNI-12); pain moves the share or the machine choice (VOL-03).

6. Session order (COACH-ANSWER ATH-11, ORD-01..03, ORD-08): warm-up -> CORE FIRST (movable) -> plyo / ballistics -> Olympic / power -> main strength lift -> resistance accessories -> isolation (calves 3 sets every leg day, rear-delt work inside the shoulders group - VOL-17, COACH-R3 VOL-01); hip-dominant with push, knee-dominant with pull (UNI-11 / ORD-06); heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days (COACH-R2 SES-01); fighters open conditioning days with a real aerobic block (ORD-09).

7. Session caps (COACH-ANSWER VOL-08 / VOL-16 / VOL-17 / UNI-09): resistance-only 5-7 exercises; field athletes off-season up to 12 + the 2-exercise core block (COACH-R2 SES-04) with 2-4 exercises for each group trained that day - cross pattern (default): 2 jump / throw stations + 1 Olympic lift; same-pattern athletic template (size-focused / high-level): 3-4 jump stations + 1 Olympic lift (COACH-R3 SES-01); about 1.5 h for athletes, bodybuilders and powerlifters (max 2 h), 45-60 min for general / weight-loss clients, 35-45 min bootcamps. Over budget -> supersets (ORD-05: also a fatigue tool) or fewer sets per slot, never drop the athletic prefix of an athlete profile. Over the EXERCISE cap -> consolidate athletic work into fewer exercises with more sets, a separate speed block for COD / sprint, supersets for calves / rear delts / arms, Focus on optional days (PROPOSED, session_load_check).

8. Fill each slot with a DEFAULT exercise plus a dropdown of same-category swaps (GEN-04), filtered by level, equipment (no bands / variable resistance - EQ-01 / EQ-12), age and injury rules (older / injured / high-volume -> constrained machines; never OHS, snatch, low-bar squat, depth jumps - EQ-03), and client preference (EQ-10). Hard rules (GEN-08) + coach-added rules.

9. Dose reps by category and rep zone (VOL 1 / 2 / 3 per block for athletes - PER-11; STRENGTH; POWER; MYO last - VOL-15; RIR primary - VOL-13); athletic slots in contacts / throws / cuts / metres; no deload inside a block (COACH-R2 VOL-07); tests chosen by checkbox at block start, or none (PER-07).

10. Audit: muscle sets vs targets (helpers 0.25, athletic sets excluded - VOL-09 / VOL-10); plyometric contacts vs the ATH-02 ranking band; all jump contacts vs the NSCA per-session guide; throws vs the ATH-05 tier; aerobic sessions 3 / 2 / 4 (+ walks) by population (ATH-07); estimated minutes vs the session-length cap.

session_load_check.heuristic: PROPOSED: 2 sets per athletic, core, isolation or focus exercise and 3 per compound (VOL-16 defaults); a medball 'Throwing' block = 1 exercise per main day (LIB-22); Focus on optional days when the profile has them (ORD-10); minutes add 50% time to unilateral lower sets (UNI-09)
session_load_check.caps: athletes with a power block 12 exercises (VOL-08 'max maybe 12', VOL-17 composition); resistance-only 5-7 + 1 core-first exercise = 8 (VOL-08 / VOL-16 / ATH-11); time 90 min athletes / bodybuilders / powerlifters (max 120), 45-60 min general and weight-loss clients (UNI-09)
session_load_check.fat_loss_minutes: about 62 min (67 with unilateral time) - over the 60 min weight-loss cap; its circuit stations are finishers (PRG-11)
session_load_check.assembly_rule_when_over: PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL: (1) consolidate - 3 sets on fewer plyo / ballistic / Olympic exercises instead of 2 sets on more (same weekly dose); (2) run COD and SPRINT as their own speed block in the fixed order squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity (LIB-21), on a separate day or as the extension of the warm-up; (3) superset calves, rear delts and arm isolation with the main lifts (ORD-05); (4) move Focus and extra isolation to the optional days (ORD-10); never drop core-first or the athletic prefix
session_load_check.caps_v1_1: field athletes: up to 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block (COACH-R2 SES-04); warm-up drills never count; a superset of two small isolations counts as one; full-body days 2-4 exercises per muscle trained that day, never 1, even if the day gets longer (COACH-R2 SES-05)
session_load_check.caps_v1_2: v1.2: 2-4 exercises for each FOCUS group trained that day (hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = all delts; COACH-R3 SES-01); field athletes inside 12 + 2 core: cross pattern (default) = 2 jump / throw stations + 1 Olympic lift, same-pattern athletic template (size-focused / high-level) = 3-4 jump stations + 1 Olympic lift; when the time cannot hold the minimums the plan says so up front, offers another day or longer sessions, then trains fewer groups directly (big movers first), recommends supersets and keeps the stairway climbing on the trained groups; never 2-4 exercises per group squeezed into a day that cannot hold them (COACH-R3 SES-02; 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.10.1)

headline_findings_v1_1: Coverage: 49 picker sports (44 with own profiles, 5 routed to the nearest profile) + 17 recreational activities + 4 age overlays -> 124 profiles; every popular US sport in the coach request and the whole gen-pop "stay athletic and active" set is present (coverage.all_present = True).

Swimming is first-class: sprint / middle / distance profiles with stroke variants, 0 extra gym cardio (the pool is the aerobic work), class 5 (25 % plyometric - starts and turns are single big efforts; v1.1 sport verification), shoulder care every session, no bands; diving and water polo alongside.

Pickleball and HYROX exist twice: recreational (rec_pickleball, hyrox_fitness - the gen-pop path the coach asked for) and competitive (pickleball_competitive with a 60+ senior variant, hyrox_competitive).

Every profile now follows the approved round-2 numbers: class shares (R2-ATH-01), aerobic counts (R2-ATH-06), in-season reductions (R2-ATH-07), pre-season about 60 % (R2-PER-06), Olympic lifts up to 4x / week with 60+ / youth rules (R2-ATH-04 / 08), spine rule (R2-SES-01/02), glute credits (R2-VOL-05).

The coach-derived 04 numbers are untouched for the sports he covered (weekly sets identical); the only 04 number changes come from newer round-2 rules (aerobic counts, glute credit, weekend-warrior resistance rebased on R2-SES-05).

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

Wed - full body B: core -> medball step-back rotational passes -> DB snatch -> trap-bar deadlift (axial day 2) + DB press -> ipsilateral 'GET OUT OF THE HIP' step-ups (trail leg) -> lateral lunges -> grip / wrist extensors -> rear delts
Fri - full body C: core -> CMJ / box jump (RC stage) -> belt squat or leg press (non-axial) + pull-ups -> single-leg RDL + landmine press -> thoracic rotation mobility -> calves
Tue / Thu / Sat - practice / rounds; aerobic 3 (walking 18 holes = Orange)

rules: rotation trained both directions; anti-rotation static before dynamic (LOW_BACK_ROTATIONAL)
between blocks the tool may change one detail of a library exercise (hand, grip, stance, implement, range) and show it as a named variation; it never invents exercises (COACH-R2 LIB-01)

every week a step up the stairway (smaller steps early, slightly bigger after halfway, hardest weeks last); no deload or maintenance week inside a block - a block that cannot be finished is cancelled, then maintenance, then a new block (COACH-R2 PER-03/04/05, VOL-07)

derived.floor_10_note: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle': muscles listed here sit under 10 in this off-season athletic budget (athletic sets never count - VOL-10). Open question O1: does the floor apply to an athlete's non-priority muscles? Until answered the volume engine lifts the sport's PRIME muscles (resistance.priorities) to >= 10 and leaves the rest as listed (PROPOSED). v1.2: SUPERSEDED in v1.2 by derived.v1_2_group_audit: the floor of 10 is counted on focus groups (hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts) in training blocks; rear delts are not a muscle with their own floor and were removed from the legacy per-muscle lists (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01)
derived.derived_note: computed with the 04 v1 nominal reps per set (PLYO 8 contacts x (1 - landing share), JLK 20, BALL 5, THROW 10, COD 7, SPRINT 60 m, TE 4) and the generator credit map (helpers 0.25; BHD/UHD glutes 0.25 per COACH-R2 VOL-05; athletic sets credit no muscle - VOL-10). Muscle targets themselves come from the volume engine (12 / 03).

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

off_season: Mon - knee + pull: warm-up -> core 2 x 2 light (COACH-R2 SES-03) -> medball list part 1 (rotational throws both sides, 1 x 10 each - LIB-22) -> ballistic jump (single-leg box jumps / broad jumps) -> clean variant (hang power clean, squat pattern - COACH-R2 ATH-04) -> HEAVY SQUAT (front / goblet squat) (axial day 1, COACH-R2 SES-01) + row -> contralateral split squat + pull-ups -> Copenhagen plank -> calves 3 sets

Tue - conditioning first: a real aerobic block (Orange 20-40 min; ORD-09) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo (switch-kick hops, skips, rope, by Receive-Create stage) -> snatch variant (DB snatch, hinge pattern) -> non-axial hinge (hip thrust / back extension / reverse hyper) + alternating DB press (reduced, not cut - ATH-04) -> single-leg RDL -> neck isometrics 4-way (clinch) + loaded hip flexion -> rear delts (in the shoulders group - COACH-R3 VOL-01) -> calves
Wed - Muay Thai / kickboxing practice; optional Focus / core day (optional days ideally separate - ORD-10)

Thu - knee + pull: core 2 x 2 -> medball list part 2 -> loaded jump (hex-bar / DB jump, 10-20 % body weight - EQ-15) -> clean variant -> belt squat or leg press (non-axial) + single-arm row -> lateral lunge / cossack (UNI-12) -> leg extensions / leg curls -> calves

Fri - conditioning first (Green 3-min rounds, a different colour from Tuesday) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo -> hang power clean -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) -> unilateral hinge -> rear delts + side raises -> calves
Sat - sparring; Sun - off; the 3rd (and 4th) aerobic session = the colour not used yet, after practice
pre_season: Camp / pre-competition block: 4-6 weeks at about 60 % of the off-season sets, more speed and power (COACH-R2 PER-06); 3 lifts (Mon / Wed / Fri) around sport sessions
Mon: core 2 x 2 -> medball list (fast) -> ballistic jump -> clean variant 3-5 reps fast -> HEAVY SQUAT 3-5 reps (axial day 1) + row -> contralateral split squat -> calves

Wed: real aerobic block first -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo (stage held) -> snatch variant -> belt squat / hip thrust (non-axial) + alternating DB press (reduced, not cut - ATH-04) -> neck isometrics 4-way (clinch) + loaded hip flexion -> calves
Fri: core 2 x 2 -> medball list -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) + broad jumps -> unilateral hinge -> rear delts + side raises -> calves
last 1-2 weeks before the event = taper (volume -40-60 %, intensity kept, no new exercises - COACH-R2 PER-06; length modifiable)
in_season: Fight week: Mon hard lift, Wed short lift, no lifting on weigh-in or fight day

Hard lift (>= 48 h before a bout / match - COACH-R2 ATH-07 extended, INFERRED): core 2 x 2 -> medball 3-4 throws x 10 -> Olympic light 2 x 3 (hang power clean or DB snatch, COACH-R2 ATH-04) -> squat OR deadlift (alternate weeks; 3-5 reps, RIR 2-3; bilateral kept minimal - UNI-10) + row -> 1 unilateral -> calves
Short lift: core 2 x 2 -> unilateral + upper push / pull 2 sets (pressing reduced, not cut) -> neck + hip flexor
Event week: one short primer early in the week; no lifting on weigh-in or competition day
Aerobic: 2 a week in season (COACH-ANSWER ATH-07) - an Orange flush after bouts / hard sparring + 1 short Blue or Green
post_season: 1-2 weeks: mobility, easy Orange cardio, no athletic work (04 post_season_recovery)
then, if wanted, a maintenance phase of chosen length (a recommendation, not mandatory); when it ends the plan ends and the athlete builds the next plan in the app (COACH-R2 PER-06; COACH-R3 PER-01)
rules: power before strength; horizontal pull before vertical (ORD-01..03); hip-dominant with push, knee-dominant with pull (UNI-11)
up to 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block (COACH-R2 SES-04); muscles trained that day get 2-4 exercises (COACH-R2 SES-05 - see team.json open question O2)
KB swings are ballistic / athletic and never count as glute volume (COACH-R2 VOL-05)
between blocks the tool may change one detail of a library exercise (hand, grip, stance, implement, range) and show it as a named variation; it never invents exercises (COACH-R2 LIB-01)

every week a step up the stairway (smaller steps early, slightly bigger after halfway, hardest weeks last); no deload or maintenance week inside a block - a block that cannot be finished is cancelled, then maintenance, then a new block (COACH-R2 PER-03/04/05, VOL-07)

no check-ins and no tracking: the plan is printed once with its planned stairway and the person or coach adjusts it ahead of time (COACH-R3 VOL-02, VOL-04); no sleep / stress / life inputs (COACH-R2 GEN-04)

off_season: Mon - knee + pull: warm-up -> core 2 x 2 light (COACH-R2 SES-03) -> medball list part 1 (rotational throws both sides, 1 x 10 each - LIB-22) -> ballistic jump (single-leg box jumps / broad jumps) -> clean variant (hang clean / KB squat clean, squat pattern - COACH-R2 ATH-04) -> HEAVY SQUAT (goblet / front squat; karate keeps bilateral low - 30/70 -> 20/80) (axial day 1, COACH-R2 SES-01) + row -> contralateral split squat + pull-ups -> Copenhagen plank -> calves 3 sets

Tue - conditioning first: a real aerobic block (Orange 20-30 min; ORD-09) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo (low-amplitude stance bounce, skips, single-leg hops, by Receive-Create stage) -> snatch variant (DB snatch / jump shrug, hinge pattern) -> non-axial hinge (hip thrust / back extension / reverse hyper) + alternating DB press (reduced when striking volume is high - ATH-04 extended) -> single-leg RDL -> loaded hip flexion (Focus) + hamstring length-strength (RDL eccentrics) -> rear delts (in the shoulders group - COACH-R3 VOL-01) -> calves
Wed - karate practice; optional Focus / core day (optional days ideally separate - ORD-10)

Thu - knee + pull: core 2 x 2 -> medball list part 2 -> loaded jump (hex-bar / DB jump, 10-20 % body weight - EQ-15) -> clean variant -> belt squat or leg press (non-axial) + single-arm row -> lateral lunge / cossack (UNI-12) -> leg extensions / leg curls -> calves

Fri - conditioning first (Blue efforts ~8-10 s at 1:1-1:4, a different colour from Tuesday) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo -> hang power clean -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) -> unilateral hinge -> side raises + rear delts -> calves
Sat - kumite / practice; Sun - off; the 3rd (and 4th) aerobic session = the colour not used yet, after practice
pre_season: Camp / pre-competition block: 4-6 weeks at about 60 % of the off-season sets, more speed and power (COACH-R2 PER-06); 3 lifts (Mon / Wed / Fri) around sport sessions
Mon: core 2 x 2 -> medball list (fast) -> ballistic jump -> clean variant 3-5 reps fast -> HEAVY SQUAT 3-5 reps (axial day 1) + row -> contralateral split squat -> calves

Wed: real aerobic block first -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo (stage held) -> snatch variant -> belt squat / hip thrust (non-axial) + alternating DB press (reduced when striking volume is high - ATH-04 extended) -> loaded hip flexion (Focus) + hamstring length-strength (RDL eccentrics) -> calves
Fri: core 2 x 2 -> medball list -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) + broad jumps -> unilateral hinge -> side raises + rear delts -> calves
last 1-2 weeks before the event = taper (volume -40-60 %, intensity kept, no new exercises - COACH-R2 PER-06; length modifiable)
in_season: Tournament blocks: Mon hard lift, Wed short lift, tournaments on weekends

Hard lift (>= 48 h before a bout / match - COACH-R2 ATH-07 extended, INFERRED): core 2 x 2 -> medball 3-4 throws x 10 -> Olympic light 2 x 3 (hang power clean or DB snatch, COACH-R2 ATH-04) -> squat OR deadlift (alternate weeks; 3-5 reps, RIR 2-3; bilateral kept minimal - UNI-10) + row -> 1 unilateral -> calves
Short lift: core 2 x 2 -> unilateral + upper push / pull 2 sets (pressing reduced) -> hip flexor + adductors
Event week: one short primer early in the week; no lifting on weigh-in or competition day
Aerobic: 2 a week in season (COACH-ANSWER ATH-07) - an Orange flush after bouts / hard sparring + 1 short Blue or Green
post_season: 1-2 weeks: mobility, easy Orange cardio, no athletic work (04 post_season_recovery)
then, if wanted, a maintenance phase of chosen length (a recommendation, not mandatory); when it ends the plan ends and the athlete builds the next plan in the app (COACH-R2 PER-06; COACH-R3 PER-01)
rules: power before strength; horizontal pull before vertical (ORD-01..03); hip-dominant with push, knee-dominant with pull (UNI-11)
up to 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block (COACH-R2 SES-04); muscles trained that day get 2-4 exercises (COACH-R2 SES-05 - see team.json open question O2)
KB swings are ballistic / athletic and never count as glute volume (COACH-R2 VOL-05)
between blocks the tool may change one detail of a library exercise (hand, grip, stance, implement, range) and show it as a named variation; it never invents exercises (COACH-R2 LIB-01)

every week a step up the stairway (smaller steps early, slightly bigger after halfway, hardest weeks last); no deload or maintenance week inside a block - a block that cannot be finished is cancelled, then maintenance, then a new block (COACH-R2 PER-03/04/05, VOL-07)

no check-ins and no tracking: the plan is printed once with its planned stairway and the person or coach adjusts it ahead of time (COACH-R3 VOL-02, VOL-04); no sleep / stress / life inputs (COACH-R2 GEN-04)

off_season: Mon - knee + pull: warm-up -> core 2 x 2 light (COACH-R2 SES-03) -> medball list part 1 (rotational throws, overhead slams, 1 x 10 each - LIB-22) -> ballistic jump (broad jumps / box jumps) -> clean variant (hang clean -> power clean, squat pattern - COACH-R2 ATH-04) -> HEAVY SQUAT (contrast with a jump for L2+ off-season - ATH-12) (axial day 1, COACH-R2 SES-01) + row -> contralateral split squat (level changes) + pull-ups -> towel hangs / farmer holds (grip) -> calves 3 sets

Tue - conditioning first: a real aerobic block (Orange 20-40 min or Green grappling exchanges 35-75 s at ~1:1; ORD-09) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo (sprawl landings -> level-change hops -> lateral bounds, by Receive-Create stage) -> snatch variant (DB snatch, hinge pattern) -> non-axial hinge (hip thrust / back extension / reverse hyper) + alternating DB press (punching volume high: reduced, not cut - ATH-04) -> single-leg RDL -> neck isometrics 4-way -> rear delts (in the shoulders group - COACH-R3 VOL-01) -> calves
Wed - MMA practice (striking / wrestling / BJJ); optional Focus / core day (optional days ideally separate - ORD-10)

Thu - knee + pull: core 2 x 2 -> medball list part 2 -> loaded jump (hex-bar / DB jump, 10-20 % body weight - EQ-15) -> clean variant -> belt squat or leg press (non-axial) + single-arm row -> lateral lunge / cossack (UNI-12) -> leg extensions / leg curls -> calves

Fri - conditioning first (Blue striking bursts 12-24 s at 1:3-1:7, a different colour from Tuesday) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo -> power clean -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) -> unilateral hinge -> sled drag + rear delts -> calves
Sat - sparring; Sun - off; the 3rd (and 4th) aerobic session = the colour not used yet, after practice
pre_season: Camp / pre-competition block: 4-6 weeks at about 60 % of the off-season sets, more speed and power (COACH-R2 PER-06); 3 lifts (Mon / Wed / Fri) around sport sessions
Mon: core 2 x 2 -> medball list (fast) -> ballistic jump -> clean variant 3-5 reps fast -> HEAVY SQUAT 3-5 reps (axial day 1) + row -> contralateral split squat (level changes) -> calves

Wed: real aerobic block first -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo (stage held) -> snatch variant -> belt squat / hip thrust (non-axial) + alternating DB press (punching volume high: reduced, not cut - ATH-04) -> neck isometrics 4-way -> calves
Fri: core 2 x 2 -> medball list -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) + broad jumps -> unilateral hinge -> sled drag + rear delts -> calves
last 1-2 weeks before the event = taper (volume -40-60 %, intensity kept, no new exercises - COACH-R2 PER-06; length modifiable)
in_season: Fight week / dense competition: Mon hard lift, Wed short lift, no lifting on weigh-in or fight day

Hard lift (>= 48 h before a bout / match - COACH-R2 ATH-07 extended, INFERRED): core 2 x 2 -> medball 3-4 throws x 10 -> Olympic light 2 x 3 (hang power clean or DB snatch, COACH-R2 ATH-04) -> squat OR deadlift (alternate weeks; 3-5 reps, RIR 2-3; bilateral kept minimal - UNI-10) + row -> 1 unilateral -> calves
Short lift: core 2 x 2 -> unilateral + upper push / pull 2 sets (pressing reduced, not cut) -> neck + grip
Event week: one short primer early in the week; no lifting on weigh-in or competition day
Aerobic: 2 a week in season (COACH-ANSWER ATH-07) - an Orange flush after bouts / hard sparring + 1 short Blue or Green
post_season: 1-2 weeks: mobility, easy Orange cardio, no athletic work (04 post_season_recovery)
then, if wanted, a maintenance phase of chosen length (a recommendation, not mandatory); when it ends the plan ends and the athlete builds the next plan in the app (COACH-R2 PER-06; COACH-R3 PER-01)
rules: power before strength; horizontal pull before vertical (ORD-01..03); hip-dominant with push, knee-dominant with pull (UNI-11)
up to 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block (COACH-R2 SES-04); muscles trained that day get 2-4 exercises (COACH-R2 SES-05 - see team.json open question O2)
KB swings are ballistic / athletic and never count as glute volume (COACH-R2 VOL-05)

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

rules: ankle-dominant track (the 'JUMPING ANKLE' ankle-hop block C124-C136 under 'TRIPPLE EXTENSION', same list as Sheet23 'FOUNDATINONAL - AP - JUMPING LIMITED KNEE' E2:E12; lateral plate hops G50-G52) 2x/week
single-leg landings with lateral component
plyo method stage 1 first: 'STICK THE LANDING BILATERAL' -> 'UNILATERAL' -> weighted (OBSERVED ballistics tab; CAT-10)
COD 'EASY TURN' -> 'MOD. TURN' -> 'HARD TURN' only after landing competency
single-leg strength + hip abductor work every week

pull sets >= push sets every week (rows before pulldowns - ORD-01); rear-delt work every week (VOL-17) - part of the shoulders group, not a muscle with its own floor; users / coaches can add more (COACH-R3 VOL-01)
scapular / rotator-cuff work with DB, cable or KB (KB face pulls = shoulder work on pull / shoulder days - COACH-R2 LIB-04, LIB-10); never bands (EQ-01)
after a flagged sprain or dislocation: DB / landmine / neutral-grip pressing and end-range isometric holds instead of barbell bench; no behind-the-neck pressing (INFERRED)
add ISO_NECK 2x/week (isometric 4-way, then plate or manual eccentric; no bands - EQ-01) - NO library column exists: create one
progress static -> dynamic like the core plane ladder
'Coppenhaggen Plank' (R47 / O165) 3x/week pre-season, 1-2x/week in-season
adductor-integrated chops / Pallofs ('Hold object Adducted between knees'); banded adduction variants are out of scope (no bands, EQ-01 / EQ-07)
frontal / transverse unilateral work (lateral lunges, cossacks, lateral step-ups) - UNI-12
anti-rotation static first (Pallof holds BC46-BC49) before rotational dynamic (chops BC9/BC13/BC17, 'Woodchoppers', 'Cable Machine Oblique Rotations')
hip rotation (into/out-of-hip) emphasis so rotation comes from the hips, not the lumbar spine (medball half-kneeling 2x2 matrix)
avoid high-volume loaded flexion+rotation (e.g. weighted Russian twists) when back pain is flagged
COACH-ANSWER VOL-03: cut that muscle or pattern 30-50%, move it to machines or split grips, keep it moving - or drop the exercise altogether if it is too much

swap fixed-grip barbell/bar -> DB/KB/handles in the same pattern; swap bilateral -> unilateral in the same pattern (MASTER_MODEL athletic A6); keep the sets ideally, 'but you have to adjust accordingly' (UNI-08)
pain moves the bilateral : unilateral share (UNI-02)

off_season: Mon - A1 knee + pull: warm-up -> core 2 x 2 sets, light (R2-SES-03) -> 2 plyo / ballistic -> clean variant (squat pattern, R2-ATH-04) -> HEAVY SQUAT (axial day 1, R2-SES-01) + horizontal pull -> unilateral knee-dominant (contralateral load) + vertical pull -> Copenhagen plank -> calves 3 sets

Tue - B1 hip + push: speed / COD block first (squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity, LIB-21; route tree EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN, ATH-06) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo + medball throws -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> non-axial hinge (hip thrust / back extension / reverse hyper) + horizontal push -> unilateral hip-dominant + vertical push -> neck isometrics 4-way + rear delts (in the shoulders group - COACH-R3 VOL-01) -> calves 3 sets
Wed - aerobic 1 + optional Focus / core (optional days ideally separate - ORD-10)
Thu - A2 knee + pull: core 2 x 2 -> 2 plyo / ballistic -> clean variant -> leg press or belt squat (non-axial) + pull -> unilateral knee-dominant -> Copenhagen plank -> calves 3 sets

Fri - B2 hip + push: speed / COD block first (squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity, LIB-21; route tree EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN, ATH-06) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo + medball throws -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap-bar (axial day 2, R2-SES-01) + push -> unilateral hip-dominant -> neck isometrics 4-way + rear delts (in the shoulders group - COACH-R3 VOL-01) -> calves 3 sets
Sat - aerobic 2 + aerobic 3 (or after a lifting day)
Sun - off
pre_season: Mon: speed / COD block first (squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity, LIB-21; route tree EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN, ATH-06) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo (stage held) -> clean variant (heavier, fewer sets) -> HEAVY SQUAT 3-5 reps, fast intent (axial day 1) + pull -> unilateral -> calves
Wed: core 2 x 2 -> plyo + medball throws -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> belt squat / hip thrust (non-axial) + push -> unilateral -> Copenhagen plank

Fri: speed / COD block first (squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity, LIB-21; route tree EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN, ATH-06) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo -> clean or snatch -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) + pull -> neck isometrics 4-way + rear delts (in the shoulders group - COACH-R3 VOL-01) -> calves
Tue / Thu / Sat: team practice; aerobic 2 = 1 Blue sport-specific repeat-effort session + 1 Green
about 62 % of the off-season weekly sets (target about 60 %, COACH-R2 PER-06); last 1-2 weeks = taper (volume -40-60 %, intensity kept, no new exercises)
in_season: Pattern: 1-2 games a week: MD+2 hard lift >= 48 h before the next game; MD-3 short power lift (as soccer).

Hard lift (>= 48 h before the next game, R2-ATH-07): core 2 x 2 -> 1 plyo at about half volume -> Olympic light 2 x 3 -> squat OR deadlift (alternate weeks; 3-5 reps, RIR 2-3; bilateral kept minimal - UNI-10) + pull -> 1 unilateral -> Copenhagen plank -> calves
Short lift (mid-week): core 2 x 2 -> unilateral + upper push / pull 2 sets -> neck isometrics 4-way + rear delts (in the shoulders group - COACH-R3 VOL-01)
Day after a game: Orange flush 20-30 min + mobility; game days: no lifting
Aerobic: 2 a week in season (COACH-ANSWER ATH-07) - usually the post-game Orange flush + 1 short Blue / Green if game minutes are low
post_season: 1-2 weeks: arm care / mobility / easy Orange cardio, no athletic work (04 post_season_recovery)
then, if wanted, a maintenance phase of chosen length (a recommendation, not mandatory); when it ends the plan ends and the athlete builds the next plan in the app (COACH-R2 PER-06; COACH-R3 PER-01)
rules: power before strength; horizontal pull before vertical (ORD-01..03); hip-dominant with push, knee-dominant with pull (UNI-11)
up to 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block (R2-SES-04); muscles trained that day get 2-4 exercises (R2-SES-05 - see open question O2)
every week a step up the stairway; no deload or maintenance week inside the block (R2-PER-03/04, R2-VOL-07)

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math
