rules: pull sets at least 1.5 x push sets every dryland week; horizontal pull before vertical pull (ORD-01); rear-delt work every week (VOL-17) - part of the shoulders group, not a muscle with its own floor; users / coaches can add more (COACH-R3 VOL-01)

swimmers: shoulder care in EVERY dryland session - external rotation (side-lying DB), prone floor Y / T raises (R2-LIB-07) and KB face pulls (R2-LIB-04, LIB-10), never bands (COACH-R3 ATH-01; EQ-01); the other sports on this list: posterior cuff and scapular work 2-3 x / week (INFERRED)

pressing = push-up variations (hands on bench = foundational, feet on bench = advanced - R2-LIB-05), neutral-grip DB or landmine press; overhead pressing low volume and seated (seated machine shoulder press - R2-LIB-07) when needed; no behind-the-neck pressing (INFERRED)

the pool is part of the load: the dryland stairway is printed once and runs as planned (no check-ins - COACH-R3 VOL-02, VOL-04); in a heavy pool week the swimmer or coach lightens dryland themselves: switch off that day's athletic block, remove a set or an exercise (COACH-R3 SES-02) - no yardage or lifestyle questions are asked (COACH-R2 GEN-04)
pec-minor / thoracic mobility in the warm-up; a stiff, rounded posture plus tight pec minor is a known risk sign (AQ13)

shoulder pain -> the swimmer or coach applies COACH-ANSWER VOL-03 on the printed plan (cut that pattern 30-50 %, move it to machines or split grips) and tells the swim coach / a professional (no check-ins - COACH-R3 VOL-02)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ3, AQ13, AQ16) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED from the 04 SHOULDER_* rules and COACH-ANSWER VOL-17 / EQ-01 / R2-LIB-04 / R2-LIB-07

rules: core first every session as anti-extension / anti-rotation (dead bug, plank, hollow hold) before any dynamic or extension work (ATH-11, R2-SES-03)
heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days; non-axial hinge (hip thrust, back extension to neutral, reverse hyper), leg press or belt squat on the other days (COACH-R2 SES-01/02)
no loaded end-range spinal extension (no hyperextension past neutral, no heavy good-morning grinders) for athletes with extension pain (INFERRED)
hip-flexor length and glute strength every week so extension comes from the hips (INFERRED)
a young athlete with one-sided low back pain on extension -> stop the extension work and refer (health screen - COACH-R2 GEN-03)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ4: about 76 % lifetime low back pain in competitive swimmers, butterfly / breaststroke highest; AQ14: divers up to 89 % lifetime, spondylolysis; AQ23 pole vault) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED + COACH-R2 SES-01/02

rules: hip internal-rotation range and hip strength every week: lateral lunge, Cossack lunge, Copenhagen plank (GROIN_ADDUCTOR), hold-between-knees squats (UNI-12 frontal / transverse unilateral list)
quad strength through a pain-free range: split squats, step-ups, leg extensions / isometric holds (slow, heavy) 2 x / week
avoid deep loaded valgus positions; knees track over toes on all squats and lunges (INFERRED)

the tool asks no kick-volume or yardage questions (COACH-R2 GEN-04): frontal-plane plyos stay low-amplitude for breaststrokers and polo players; with knee pain the swimmer or coach swaps the exercise or moves the bilateral : unilateral share themselves (VOL-03, UNI-02; no check-ins - COACH-R3 VOL-02)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ4: 73-75 % of breaststrokers report knee pain; AQ16: eggbeater kick loads the medial knee and hip) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED

rules: keep some jumping all year even when the plyo share is low: ballistic jumps (squat / box / broad / hex-bar - R2-ATH-02) plus a small low-amplitude block (pogo / ankle hops) 2-3 x / week
heavy compound lifting (squat, deadlift, loaded carries) every off-season block

progress impact gradually with the Receive-Create stages (COACH-R2 ATH-03); older clients follow COACH-R2 ATH-08 (no plyos by default - landing drills OK; low ankle hops and other impact are the first opt-in items, with the warning - useful for bone)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ8: swimming is not osteogenic and a 9-month jumping programme improved bone in adolescent swimmers and cyclists; AQ30: road cyclists show low bone density, strength training helps)

rules: COACH-ANSWER VOL-03: cut that muscle or pattern 30-50%, move it to machines or split grips, keep it moving - or drop the exercise altogether if it is too much

swap fixed-grip barbell/bar -> DB/KB/handles in the same pattern; swap bilateral -> unilateral in the same pattern (MASTER_MODEL athletic A6); keep the sets ideally, 'but you have to adjust accordingly' (UNI-08)
pain moves the bilateral : unilateral share (UNI-02)

pain in an exercise -> the person or coach swaps it within the category or lowers the level (GEN-05 RIGHT); if it keeps hurting: swap, then cut sets, then drop a library level (INFERRED order) - done on the printed plan; no pain reports are collected or stored (COACH-R3 VOL-02, GEN-01; editing COACH-R3 SES-02)
all prehab uses DB, KB, cable, machine, bodyweight or plates - never bands, chains or variable resistance (COACH-ANSWER EQ-01, EQ-12)
'Coppenhaggen Plank' (R47 / O165) 3x/week pre-season, 1-2x/week in-season
adductor-integrated chops / Pallofs ('Hold object Adducted between knees'); banded adduction variants are out of scope (no bands, EQ-01 / EQ-07)
frontal / transverse unilateral work (lateral lunges, cossacks, lateral step-ups) - UNI-12

age_notes: high school, college and pro: same plan; loads and speeds change, pros get more care for their bodies (COACH-ANSWER PRG-09)
youth: Olympic lifts from the floor from about 14, after one block of hang work; younger / growth-spurt athletes follow youth_athlete rules (COACH-R2 ATH-08, COACH-ANSWER ATH-09)

60+: no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default; offered as an option with 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means' (COACH-R2 ATH-08); landing drills (step-down and stick, no rebound) still fine; low ankle hops join the opt-in (they are on the plyometric list - COACH-R2 ATH-02); constrained machines for compounds and isolation (EQ-03)
more than 6-12 months off: the body is treated as L1 (PRG-05)
no rule depends on sex (ATH-09)

age-group swimmers (USA Swimming 10 & under to 15-18): pool loads are already high (AQ12) - dryland uses foundational lists (bodyweight, DB, light medball), landing skills and cuff work; floor Olympic lifts from about 14 after a hang block (COACH-R2 ATH-08)
high school / college: same plan, loads and speeds differ (PRG-09); college swimmers carry the biggest pool loads, so dryland stays 45-75 min

masters (US Masters Swimming, 18+): shoulder pain peaks at 40-60 (AQ13); bone loading and strength matter more with age (AQ8, AQ41); from 60 the older rules apply (no Olympic lifts / plyos / depth jumps by default, optional with the warning - COACH-R2 ATH-08)
equipment: full gym or DB / KB gym (often a pool-deck dryland room)
boxes for box jumps and step-ups
cable or DB for cuff work
no bands / variable resistance (EQ-01, EQ-12) - most swim dryland uses bands; every band move has a DB / cable / KB swap in 10_equipment_model

off_season: Mon - A knee + pull (before or after a pool session, >= 4 h apart when possible): warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip or mobility; never counted - ORD-08) -> core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> box jump / squat jump (BALL) -> hang clean (squat pattern, R2-ATH-04) -> HEAVY SQUAT 3-5 reps (axial day 1 - COACH-R2 SES-01) + chest-supported / 1-arm DB row -> rear-foot-elevated split squat (staggered = kick-start stance) + pull-up or lat pulldown -> side-lying DB external rotation + KB face pulls (shoulder work, R2-LIB-04) -> calves 3 sets

Wed - B hip + push: warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip or mobility; never counted - ORD-08) -> core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> medball overhead throw + rotational scoop toss -> single-arm DB snatch (hinge pattern, single-arm DB snatch by default for swimmers - INFERRED) -> hip thrust / back extension to neutral (non-axial) + push-ups (hands on bench -> feet on bench, R2-LIB-05) -> single-leg RDL + neutral-grip DB press -> Nordic or slider curls -> side-lying DB external rotation + prone floor Y / T raises (shoulder care every dryland session, never bands - COACH-R3 ATH-01) -> calves 3 sets

Fri - C full: warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip or mobility; never counted - ORD-08) -> core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> ballistic jumps from a streamline / deep start position + pogo hops (bone loading - AQ8) -> hex-bar jump or hang clean -> HEAVY trap-bar DEADLIFT 3-5 reps (axial day 2) + straight-arm pull-over (pull under, LIB-09) -> lateral lunge (frontal plane) + DB row -> triceps (streamline lockout) + prone floor Y / T raises (R2-LIB-07) -> calves 3 sets
Sat or after any pool session (optional Focus day, ORD-10): rotator cuff, scapular stabilisers, hip IR / adductors (Copenhagen) for IM and breaststroke
pool practices on the other sessions (the swim coach's plan = the aerobic work); 2-4 exercises per muscle trained that day (COACH-R2 SES-05) - lats and quads get 2 each on A, chest 2 on B
pre_season: Mon: core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> box jump / squat jump (BALL) (fewer, max intent) -> hang clean heavier, fewer sets -> HEAVY SQUAT 3-5 reps fast intent (axial 1) + row -> split squat -> cuff work

Thu: core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> medball overhead throw + rotational scoop toss -> single-arm DB snatch -> trap-bar deadlift 3 x 3 fast (axial 2) + push-ups -> single-leg RDL -> Y / T raises -> calves
optional third short lift (Fri: core -> jumps 2 x 3 -> 1 lower + 1 pull -> cuff work) or a Focus session (cuff / scap / hips) 20 min

about 60 % of the off-season dryland sets, more speed and power (COACH-R2 PER-06); before the first (smaller) meets a 1-week dryland taper or none; the 2-week taper is kept for the main championship meet (COACH-R3 ATH-01)
in_season: 2 lifts (e.g. Mon / Wed with a Saturday meet - the harder lift >= 48 h before the meet): core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> 1 ballistic jump (3 x 3) -> hang clean 2 x 3 (R2-ATH-04) -> squat or trap-bar 2-3 x 3 at about 80 % effort -> 1 pull + 1 push -> cuff work
Fri (day before a meet): nothing heavy; optional 10 min core / cuff activation

championship taper (the 2 weeks before the main championship meet, lined up with the swim coach's taper; 1 week or none before smaller meets - COACH-R3 ATH-01): dryland volume -40-60 %, keep intensity, last heavy lift 7-10 days out, short power primer (2-3 jumps x 3, 1 x 2 hang clean) up to ~4-5 days out (AQ7; timing INFERRED)
sample_week.shoulder_care_rule: every dryland day (A, B, C and the pre- / in-season lifts) carries shoulder care: external rotation, floor Y / T raises or KB face pulls, never bands (COACH-R3 ATH-01)

menu: countermovement jump or standing broad jump (start power - AQ6)
strength: 5-8RM (beginners) / 3RM or work up to a 1RM (intermediate+) on squat or trap-bar deadlift and a pull (pull-up reps or DB row RM)
pool tests (times, 15 m start, turns) belong to the swim coach, not to the tool
tests.timing: before the block (or week 1) and in the last week, never mid-block; the plan prints the test days with a 'get ready' line 7 days before and the day before - no stored data or push reminders (COACH-R2 PER-07; COACH-R3 GEN-01)
tests.safety: people starting from zero never test a 1RM or a max-effort mile / time trial: 5RM / 3RM or 80-90 % efforts instead (COACH-R2 PER-07)
tests.sport_note: no gym 'cardio' test for swimmers - the pool supplies it; untrained swimmers never test a 1RM from zero (COACH-R2 PER-07)

season_calendar_us.club_usa_swimming: two seasons a year: short course (25 yd) September-March, long course (50 m) April-early August (AQ9) -> two macrocycles, each ending in a championship meet + taper
season_calendar_us.high_school: about 12-16 weeks; winter (Nov-Feb/Mar) in most states, fall (Aug-Nov) in some states or for one sex (AQ10); dual meets 1-2 a week, conference / state at the end
season_calendar_us.college: practice from September; dual meets Oct-Jan; conference championships mid-late February; NCAA Championships mid-late March (AQ11)
season_calendar_us.pro_national: long-course summer peak (nationals / trials / internationals Jun-Aug)

sport_load_context.dryland_vs_pool: the pool is the sport AND the aerobic work: the tool adds 0 aerobic colour sessions by default (adjustable, COACH-R2 SES-06); dryland = strength, power, start / turn ballistics, shoulder health and bone loading

The tool asks no yardage or lifestyle questions (COACH-R2 GEN-04) and has no check-ins (COACH-R3 VOL-02): the whole dryland plan is printed ahead and the swimmer or coach lightens a heavy pool week themselves (switch off the athletic block, remove sets or exercises - COACH-R3 SES-02); O5 closed by round 3

profiles.stairway: every block climbs like a stairway: smaller steps in the first weeks, slightly bigger after the halfway point, the hardest weeks last (12-week: last 4 weeks 'brutal'); 'start at a 2, end at an 11' = perceived effort / overall load, not set counts; no deload or maintenance week inside a block (COACH-R2 PER-03/04/05, VOL-07)

profiles.season_model: swimming has no classic off-season: each season (short course and long course) is a macrocycle - general prep ('off-season' block in the tool, 6-12 weeks) -> specific prep ('pre-season' block, 4-6 weeks, about 60 % of off-season dryland sets, more speed and power - COACH-R2 PER-06) -> competition ('in-season', 2 lifts a week) -> championship taper: 2 weeks of dryland taper lined up with the pool taper before the main championship meet, 1 week or none before smaller meets (COACH-R3 ATH-01; SCIENCE AQ7) -> 1-3 weeks transition (a maintenance block - COACH-R2 VOL-07 / PER-06). Club swimmers run this twice a year; high-school-only swimmers once (INFERRED)

dryland_realism_v1_1.pool_load: the pool supplies the aerobic work (elite about 40-70 km a week - AQ12): 0 extra gym aerobic sessions by default; the user can add one (COACH-R3 ATH-01, ATH-04; COACH-R2 SES-06); an optional land Orange only in the transition block
dryland_realism_v1_1.dryland_days: 3 dryland gym days + 1 optional around pool training; 2 for younger or lower-level swimmers (COACH-R3 ATH-01; 'younger' = under about 14 or L1 - PROPOSED); each >= 4 h from a hard pool set when possible (INFERRED)
dryland_realism_v1_1.focus: strength and power for starts and turns (lower-body max strength and jump power relate to 15 m start time - West et al. 2011, r = -0.74 to -0.85, AQ6) + shoulder health every session + trunk
dryland_realism_v1_1.plyo: jump work mostly ballistic: 25 % plyometric at the end of a block (class 5; start 10 %), because starts and turns are single big efforts (COACH-R3 ATH-01, ATH-04); ballistic jumps from a start / streamline position; small ankle block for bone (AQ8); no depth jumps, bounds or hurdle hops by default
dryland_realism_v1_1.shoulder: shoulder care in every dryland session: external rotation, floor Y / T raises, KB face pulls - never bands (COACH-R3 ATH-01); low-volume, seated or landmine overhead pressing; overhead medball throws kept off heavy-pull pool days; snatch variants single-arm DB first
dryland_realism_v1_1.taper: a 2-week dryland taper lined up with the swim coach's pool taper before the main championship meet; 1 week or none before smaller meets (COACH-R3 ATH-01); the swim coach tapers the pool, the tool tapers dryland only
dryland_realism_v1_1.evidence: COACH-R3 ATH-01 (approved dryland defaults: days, cardio, plyo share, Olympic days, shoulder care, taper); SCIENCE AQ6 / AQ7 / AQ8 / AQ12; v1.1 sport verification
dryland_realism_v1_1.olympic: Olympic lifts 2-3 days a week (COACH-R3 ATH-01): sprint and middle-distance 3 by default, distance 2

v1_2_round3: COACH-R3 ATH-01 approved the dryland defaults: 3 dryland gym days + 1 optional around pool training (2 for younger or lower-level swimmers); 0 extra gym cardio (the pool is the aerobic work; the user can add one); jump work mostly ballistic, 25 % plyometric at the end of a block; Olympic lifts 2-3 days (this profile: 3); shoulder care (external rotation, floor Y / T raises, KB face pulls) every session, never bands; a 2-week dryland taper lined up with the swim coach's taper before the main championship meet, 1 week or none before smaller meets
sample week fixed in v1.2: the B (hip + push) day and the optional third pre-season lift now carry shoulder care too, so every dryland session has it
no check-ins (COACH-R3 VOL-02): the whole dryland plan is printed ahead; in a heavy pool week the swimmer or coach switches off that day's athletic block or removes sets (COACH-R3 SES-02)

plyo.phases: Receive-Create stages: 12-week plan RC1 Land wk 1-3, RC2 Land & Go wk 4-7, RC3 Repeat wk 8-12; 8-week plan 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8; restart at stage 1 each off-season; stay at the current stage in maintenance blocks; L2-L3 may start at stage 2 (COACH-R2 ATH-03); the purpose is bone loading and turn power, not elasticity
lists: ballistic = squat jumps, box jumps, broad jumps, loaded / hex-bar jumps, medball throws (COACH-R2 ATH-02)
plyometric = pogo / ankle hops, hurdle hops, depth jumps, bounds, squirrel jumps, repeated jumps (COACH-R2 ATH-02)

pre_season.evidence: COACH-R2 PER-06 (4-6 weeks at about 60 % of off-season sets, more speed and power, 1-2-week taper; modifiable); category factors PROPOSED, resistance factor solved so the week lands at about 60 % (floor 0.25); core and calves follow the number of lift days (core 2 x 2 per session - R2-SES-03; calves 3 sets per leg day - VOL-17)

v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)

ground_contact.label: very long / grounded
ground_contact.typical: no ground contact in the race: the decisive pushes are single big efforts - the block start (about 0.70-0.80 s on the block - AQ1) and wall push-offs on turns (about 0.3 s - AQ2); one big effort with a long contact = BALLISTIC in the coach's own definition (COACH-R2 ATH-02), and the sport has no repeated bouncing contacts at all -> the 'very long / single-effort' class 5, like water polo (v1.1 sport verification; was class 4 / 40 %)
ground_contact.evidence: COACH-R3 ATH-01 and ATH-04 (approved: swimming 25 % plyometric at the end of a block - jump work mostly ballistic because starts and turns are single big efforts); block / wall contact times AQ1, AQ2, S32; contact-time rule COACH-ANSWER ATH-01; the small plyometric part is kept for bone (AQ8) and is mostly low-amplitude ankle work (JLK)
ground_contact.examples: boxing, karate, kickboxing, golf, wrestling, BJJ; swimming and water polo (single big efforts in the water - v1.1)

olympic_policy.rule: everyone in athletic training gets Olympic lifts (COACH-ANSWER ATH-10)
olympic_policy.pattern_split: clean variants on knee / squat days, snatch variants on hip / hinge days - cleans read as more squat-pattern, snatches more hinge-pattern; up to 4 exposures a week (COACH-R2 ATH-04)
olympic_policy.reps: full squat cleans / snatches 3-5 reps per set at the same weekly reps, coach's eye on speed (COACH-R2 ATH-05); DB / KB and pull variants may use the 4 x 8 @75 % -> 4 x 4 @90 % ramp (PER-09)
olympic_policy.load_guidance: RIR / RPE; explained as power output; % only for competitive Olympic lifters, which is its own programming (COACH-R2 GEN-06)
olympic_policy.pre_season: kept, fewer sets, faster - more speed and power (COACH-R2 PER-06)
olympic_policy.in_season: light 2 x 3 (hang power clean or DB snatch) on 1-2 gym days; dropped in heavy competition weeks (COACH-R2 ATH-04)
olympic_policy.contrast: French contrast / complexes for L2+ in the off-season only, heavy lift about 78-85 % (ATH-12)
olympic_policy.youth: floor lifts from about 14, after one block of hang work (COACH-R2 ATH-08)
olympic_policy.older_60_plus: none by default; offered as an option with the warning 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means' (COACH-R2 ATH-08); older / injured / high-volume clients never get snatch variants (EQ-03)
olympic_policy.sport_note: low dose (2 exposures): hex-bar jumps, hang pulls, KB squat clean; single-arm DB snatch only with healthy shoulders
olympic_policy.v1_1_verification_note: barbell snatch variants removed from the distance-swimmer L2+ list so it matches resistance.avoid ('barbell snatch') and the high-shoulder-volume rule (EQ-03 logic); cleans, pulls and hex-bar jumps lead
olympic_policy.frequency_r3: Olympic lifts 2-3 days a week for swimmers (COACH-R3 ATH-01); this profile: 2

medball_policy.types: overhead throws and slams (streamline / catch line), rotational scoop tosses for long-axis strokes; 4-8 lb; overhead throws kept off heavy-pull pool days
medball_policy.level: low (INFERRED - swimming is not on the ATH-05 list)
medball_policy.loads_lb: passes / rotations 8-10 (speed), slams 10-20, overhead 6-10, sit-up throws 6-8; never over 20 lb; lighter for youth and older clients (COACH-ANSWER EQ-06)
medball_policy.no_ball: plyo push-ups (pressing), fast cable rotations or the 'fake medball slam'; never band chops (COACH-ANSWER EQ-07)
medball_policy.dose_unit: 1 x 10 per throw; a throwing slot can be the whole ~19-throw 'ALL LIST' (LIB-22)
medball_policy.in_season: x0.5 in season (PROPOSED)
medball_policy.aesthetics_rule: not an aesthetics profile, so throws may stay in the main workout (COACH-ANSWER ATH-05: none for aesthetics)
medball_policy.counts_as: ballistic side of the plyo : ballistic split (04 / BRAIN 9.6)

in_season_gym.lift_days_evidence: COACH-ANSWER PER-08 (about 2 lifting days, low volume)
in_season_gym.hard_day_rule: the harder lift >= 48 h before a meet (COACH-R2 ATH-07 spacing applied to meets - INFERRED extension)
in_season_gym.default_pattern: Saturday meet: lifts Monday (harder) and Wednesday (short power / maintenance); Friday = rest or 10 min activation
in_season_gym.game_heavy_evidence: swimming is not on the COACH-R2 ATH-07 list; meets give no land jumps or sprints, so gym jumps are NOT halved for that reason - they drop only because of the in-season volume cut (INFERRED)

taper.length_weeks: 2 before the main championship meet, lined up with the swim coach's taper; 1 week or none before smaller meets (COACH-R3 ATH-01)
taper.primer: very low-volume jumps / hang cleans until ~4-5 days out (INFERRED)
taper.pool: the swim coach tapers the pool; the tool only tapers dryland

in_season_gym.intake: COACH-R2 GEN-05 (season start date + practice / meet days) + the main championship meet date (and optionally smaller meet dates) so the 2-week dryland taper lands on the swim coach's taper (COACH-R3 ATH-01)
in_season_gym.typical_games_wk: 1-2 dual / invitational meets a week in season; championship meets at the end (AQ10, AQ11)
in_season_gym.game_heavy_basis: not game-heavy: in-season = about 2 lifting days, low volume (COACH-ANSWER PER-08)

rules: pull sets at least 1.5 x push sets every dryland week; horizontal pull before vertical pull (ORD-01); rear-delt work every week (VOL-17) - part of the shoulders group, not a muscle with its own floor; users / coaches can add more (COACH-R3 VOL-01)

swimmers: shoulder care in EVERY dryland session - external rotation (side-lying DB), prone floor Y / T raises (R2-LIB-07) and KB face pulls (R2-LIB-04, LIB-10), never bands (COACH-R3 ATH-01; EQ-01); the other sports on this list: posterior cuff and scapular work 2-3 x / week (INFERRED)

pressing = push-up variations (hands on bench = foundational, feet on bench = advanced - R2-LIB-05), neutral-grip DB or landmine press; overhead pressing low volume and seated (seated machine shoulder press - R2-LIB-07) when needed; no behind-the-neck pressing (INFERRED)

the pool is part of the load: the dryland stairway is printed once and runs as planned (no check-ins - COACH-R3 VOL-02, VOL-04); in a heavy pool week the swimmer or coach lightens dryland themselves: switch off that day's athletic block, remove a set or an exercise (COACH-R3 SES-02) - no yardage or lifestyle questions are asked (COACH-R2 GEN-04)
pec-minor / thoracic mobility in the warm-up; a stiff, rounded posture plus tight pec minor is a known risk sign (AQ13)

shoulder pain -> the swimmer or coach applies COACH-ANSWER VOL-03 on the printed plan (cut that pattern 30-50 %, move it to machines or split grips) and tells the swim coach / a professional (no check-ins - COACH-R3 VOL-02)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ3, AQ13, AQ16) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED from the 04 SHOULDER_* rules and COACH-ANSWER VOL-17 / EQ-01 / R2-LIB-04 / R2-LIB-07

rules: core first every session as anti-extension / anti-rotation (dead bug, plank, hollow hold) before any dynamic or extension work (ATH-11, R2-SES-03)
heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days; non-axial hinge (hip thrust, back extension to neutral, reverse hyper), leg press or belt squat on the other days (COACH-R2 SES-01/02)
no loaded end-range spinal extension (no hyperextension past neutral, no heavy good-morning grinders) for athletes with extension pain (INFERRED)
hip-flexor length and glute strength every week so extension comes from the hips (INFERRED)
a young athlete with one-sided low back pain on extension -> stop the extension work and refer (health screen - COACH-R2 GEN-03)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ4: about 76 % lifetime low back pain in competitive swimmers, butterfly / breaststroke highest; AQ14: divers up to 89 % lifetime, spondylolysis; AQ23 pole vault) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED + COACH-R2 SES-01/02

rules: hip internal-rotation range and hip strength every week: lateral lunge, Cossack lunge, Copenhagen plank (GROIN_ADDUCTOR), hold-between-knees squats (UNI-12 frontal / transverse unilateral list)
quad strength through a pain-free range: split squats, step-ups, leg extensions / isometric holds (slow, heavy) 2 x / week
avoid deep loaded valgus positions; knees track over toes on all squats and lunges (INFERRED)

the tool asks no kick-volume or yardage questions (COACH-R2 GEN-04): frontal-plane plyos stay low-amplitude for breaststrokers and polo players; with knee pain the swimmer or coach swaps the exercise or moves the bilateral : unilateral share themselves (VOL-03, UNI-02; no check-ins - COACH-R3 VOL-02)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ4: 73-75 % of breaststrokers report knee pain; AQ16: eggbeater kick loads the medial knee and hip) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED

rules: keep some jumping all year even when the plyo share is low: ballistic jumps (squat / box / broad / hex-bar - R2-ATH-02) plus a small low-amplitude block (pogo / ankle hops) 2-3 x / week
heavy compound lifting (squat, deadlift, loaded carries) every off-season block

progress impact gradually with the Receive-Create stages (COACH-R2 ATH-03); older clients follow COACH-R2 ATH-08 (no plyos by default - landing drills OK; low ankle hops and other impact are the first opt-in items, with the warning - useful for bone)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ8: swimming is not osteogenic and a 9-month jumping programme improved bone in adolescent swimmers and cyclists; AQ30: road cyclists show low bone density, strength training helps)

rules: COACH-ANSWER VOL-03: cut that muscle or pattern 30-50%, move it to machines or split grips, keep it moving - or drop the exercise altogether if it is too much

swap fixed-grip barbell/bar -> DB/KB/handles in the same pattern; swap bilateral -> unilateral in the same pattern (MASTER_MODEL athletic A6); keep the sets ideally, 'but you have to adjust accordingly' (UNI-08)
pain moves the bilateral : unilateral share (UNI-02)

pain in an exercise -> the person or coach swaps it within the category or lowers the level (GEN-05 RIGHT); if it keeps hurting: swap, then cut sets, then drop a library level (INFERRED order) - done on the printed plan; no pain reports are collected or stored (COACH-R3 VOL-02, GEN-01; editing COACH-R3 SES-02)
all prehab uses DB, KB, cable, machine, bodyweight or plates - never bands, chains or variable resistance (COACH-ANSWER EQ-01, EQ-12)
'Coppenhaggen Plank' (R47 / O165) 3x/week pre-season, 1-2x/week in-season
adductor-integrated chops / Pallofs ('Hold object Adducted between knees'); banded adduction variants are out of scope (no bands, EQ-01 / EQ-07)
frontal / transverse unilateral work (lateral lunges, cossacks, lateral step-ups) - UNI-12
injury_prehab.extension: sports added: breaststroke / IM swimmers, water polo (eggbeater; AQ17 hip / groin pain), hurdlers, skiers.

age_notes: high school, college and pro: same plan; loads and speeds change, pros get more care for their bodies (COACH-ANSWER PRG-09)
youth: Olympic lifts from the floor from about 14, after one block of hang work; younger / growth-spurt athletes follow youth_athlete rules (COACH-R2 ATH-08, COACH-ANSWER ATH-09)

60+: no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default; offered as an option with 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means' (COACH-R2 ATH-08); landing drills (step-down and stick, no rebound) still fine; low ankle hops join the opt-in (they are on the plyometric list - COACH-R2 ATH-02); constrained machines for compounds and isolation (EQ-03)
more than 6-12 months off: the body is treated as L1 (PRG-05)
no rule depends on sex (ATH-09)

age-group swimmers (USA Swimming 10 & under to 15-18): pool loads are already high (AQ12) - dryland uses foundational lists (bodyweight, DB, light medball), landing skills and cuff work; floor Olympic lifts from about 14 after a hang block (COACH-R2 ATH-08)
high school / college: same plan, loads and speeds differ (PRG-09); college swimmers carry the biggest pool loads, so dryland stays 45-75 min

masters (US Masters Swimming, 18+): shoulder pain peaks at 40-60 (AQ13); bone loading and strength matter more with age (AQ8, AQ41); from 60 the older rules apply (no Olympic lifts / plyos / depth jumps by default, optional with the warning - COACH-R2 ATH-08)
equipment: full gym or DB / KB gym (often a pool-deck dryland room)
boxes for box jumps and step-ups
cable or DB for cuff work
no bands / variable resistance (EQ-01, EQ-12) - most swim dryland uses bands; every band move has a DB / cable / KB swap in 10_equipment_model

off_season: Mon - A knee + pull (before or after a pool session, >= 4 h apart when possible): warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip or mobility; never counted - ORD-08) -> core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> squat jump / box jump (BALL, 3 x 3) -> KB squat clean / hang pull (squat pattern, R2-ATH-04) -> HEAVY SQUAT 3-5 reps (axial day 1 - COACH-R2 SES-01) + chest-supported / 1-arm DB row -> rear-foot-elevated split squat (staggered = kick-start stance) + pull-up or lat pulldown -> side-lying DB external rotation + KB face pulls (shoulder work, R2-LIB-04) -> calves 3 sets

Wed - B hip + push: warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip or mobility; never counted - ORD-08) -> core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> medball rotational scoop toss + light overhead throw -> single-arm DB snatch (or hex-bar jump) (hinge pattern, single-arm DB snatch by default for swimmers - INFERRED) -> hip thrust / back extension to neutral (non-axial) + push-ups (hands on bench -> feet on bench, R2-LIB-05) -> single-leg RDL + neutral-grip DB press -> Nordic or slider curls -> side-lying DB external rotation + prone floor Y / T raises (shoulder care every dryland session, never bands - COACH-R3 ATH-01) -> calves 3 sets

Fri - C full: warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip or mobility; never counted - ORD-08) -> core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> ballistic jumps from a streamline / deep start position + pogo hops (bone loading - AQ8) -> hex-bar jump or hang clean -> HEAVY trap-bar DEADLIFT 3-5 reps (axial day 2) + straight-arm pull-over (pull under, LIB-09) -> lateral lunge (frontal plane) + DB row -> triceps (streamline lockout) + prone floor Y / T raises (R2-LIB-07) -> calves 3 sets
Sat or after any pool session (optional Focus day, ORD-10): rotator cuff endurance (2 x 15-20 side-lying ER, prone Y / T), scapular push-up plus, hip stability
pool practices on the other sessions (the swim coach's plan = the aerobic work); 2-4 exercises per muscle trained that day (COACH-R2 SES-05) - lats and quads get 2 each on A, chest 2 on B
pre_season: Mon: core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> squat jump / box jump (BALL, 3 x 3) (fewer, max intent) -> KB squat clean / hang pull heavier, fewer sets -> HEAVY SQUAT 3-5 reps fast intent (axial 1) + row -> split squat -> cuff work

Thu: core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> medball rotational scoop toss + light overhead throw -> single-arm DB snatch (or hex-bar jump) -> trap-bar deadlift 3 x 3 fast (axial 2) + push-ups -> single-leg RDL -> Y / T raises -> calves
optional third short lift (Fri: core -> jumps 2 x 3 -> 1 lower + 1 pull -> cuff work) or a Focus session (cuff / scap / hips) 20 min

about 60 % of the off-season dryland sets, more speed and power (COACH-R2 PER-06); before the first (smaller) meets a 1-week dryland taper or none; the 2-week taper is kept for the main championship meet (COACH-R3 ATH-01)
in_season: 2 lifts (e.g. Mon / Wed with a Saturday meet - the harder lift >= 48 h before the meet): core 2 x 2 light (dead bug / hollow / side plank - ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> 1 ballistic jump (3 x 3) -> KB squat clean / hang pull 2 x 3 (R2-ATH-04) -> squat or trap-bar 2-3 x 3 at about 80 % effort -> 1 pull + 1 push -> cuff work
Fri (day before a meet): nothing heavy; optional 10 min core / cuff activation

championship taper (the 2 weeks before the main championship meet, lined up with the swim coach's taper; 1 week or none before smaller meets - COACH-R3 ATH-01): dryland volume -40-60 %, keep intensity, last heavy lift 7-10 days out, short power primer (2-3 jumps x 3, 1 x 2 hang clean) up to ~4-5 days out (AQ7; timing INFERRED)
sample_week.shoulder_care_rule: every dryland day (A, B, C and the pre- / in-season lifts) carries shoulder care: external rotation, floor Y / T raises or KB face pulls, never bands (COACH-R3 ATH-01)

menu: countermovement jump or standing broad jump (start power - AQ6)
strength: 5-8RM (beginners) / 3RM or work up to a 1RM (intermediate+) on squat or trap-bar deadlift and a pull (pull-up reps or DB row RM)
pool tests (times, 15 m start, turns) belong to the swim coach, not to the tool
tests.timing: before the block (or week 1) and in the last week, never mid-block; the plan prints the test days with a 'get ready' line 7 days before and the day before - no stored data or push reminders (COACH-R2 PER-07; COACH-R3 GEN-01)
tests.safety: people starting from zero never test a 1RM or a max-effort mile / time trial: 5RM / 3RM or 80-90 % efforts instead (COACH-R2 PER-07)

profiles.season_model: swimming has no classic off-season: each season (short course and long course) is a macrocycle - general prep ('off-season' block in the tool, 6-12 weeks) -> specific prep ('pre-season' block, 4-6 weeks, about 60 % of off-season dryland sets, more speed and power - COACH-R2 PER-06) -> competition ('in-season', 2 lifts a week) -> championship taper: 2 weeks of dryland taper lined up with the pool taper before the main championship meet, 1 week or none before smaller meets (COACH-R3 ATH-01; SCIENCE AQ7) -> 1-3 weeks transition (a maintenance block - COACH-R2 VOL-07 / PER-06). Club swimmers run this twice a year; high-school-only swimmers once (INFERRED)

dryland_realism_v1_1.pool_load: the pool supplies the aerobic work (elite about 40-70 km a week - AQ12): 0 extra gym aerobic sessions by default; the user can add one (COACH-R3 ATH-01, ATH-04; COACH-R2 SES-06); an optional land Orange only in the transition block
dryland_realism_v1_1.dryland_days: 3 dryland gym days + 1 optional around pool training; 2 for younger or lower-level swimmers (COACH-R3 ATH-01; 'younger' = under about 14 or L1 - PROPOSED); each >= 4 h from a hard pool set when possible (INFERRED)
dryland_realism_v1_1.focus: strength and power for starts and turns (lower-body max strength and jump power relate to 15 m start time - West et al. 2011, r = -0.74 to -0.85, AQ6) + shoulder health every session + trunk
dryland_realism_v1_1.plyo: jump work mostly ballistic: 25 % plyometric at the end of a block (class 5; start 10 %), because starts and turns are single big efforts (COACH-R3 ATH-01, ATH-04); ballistic jumps from a start / streamline position; small ankle block for bone (AQ8); no depth jumps, bounds or hurdle hops by default
dryland_realism_v1_1.shoulder: shoulder care in every dryland session: external rotation, floor Y / T raises, KB face pulls - never bands (COACH-R3 ATH-01); low-volume, seated or landmine overhead pressing; overhead medball throws kept off heavy-pull pool days; snatch variants single-arm DB first
dryland_realism_v1_1.taper: a 2-week dryland taper lined up with the swim coach's pool taper before the main championship meet; 1 week or none before smaller meets (COACH-R3 ATH-01); the swim coach tapers the pool, the tool tapers dryland only

profiles.rationale: Divers need maximal jump height, fast rotation (tight tuck / pike = hip-flexor and core compression strength), and overhead shoulder and wrist stability for entries. Injuries cluster at the shoulder, lumbar spine (repetitive hyperextension -> spondylolysis, LBP up to 89 % lifetime) and wrist / hand (AQ14). Land jumping volume is already high in dry-board and trampoline work, so the gym biases ballistic, low-contact jumps and strength.

pressing = push-up variations (hands on bench = foundational, feet on bench = advanced - R2-LIB-05), neutral-grip DB or landmine press; overhead pressing low volume and seated (seated machine shoulder press - R2-LIB-07) when needed; no behind-the-neck pressing (INFERRED)

the pool is part of the load: the dryland stairway is printed once and runs as planned (no check-ins - COACH-R3 VOL-02, VOL-04); in a heavy pool week the swimmer or coach lightens dryland themselves: switch off that day's athletic block, remove a set or an exercise (COACH-R3 SES-02) - no yardage or lifestyle questions are asked (COACH-R2 GEN-04)
pec-minor / thoracic mobility in the warm-up; a stiff, rounded posture plus tight pec minor is a known risk sign (AQ13)

shoulder pain -> the swimmer or coach applies COACH-ANSWER VOL-03 on the printed plan (cut that pattern 30-50 %, move it to machines or split grips) and tells the swim coach / a professional (no check-ins - COACH-R3 VOL-02)

rules: hip internal-rotation range and hip strength every week: lateral lunge, Cossack lunge, Copenhagen plank (GROIN_ADDUCTOR), hold-between-knees squats (UNI-12 frontal / transverse unilateral list)

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

no rule depends on sex (ATH-09)

Tue - hip + push: warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip / Run; A-drills never count - ORD-08) -> core 2 x 2 light (ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> medball throws + ballistic jumps (box / broad / hex-bar - R2-ATH-02) -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> hip thrust / back extension (non-axial) + DB bench -> single-leg RDL + DB overhead press -> loaded hip flexion (Focus) -> calves 3 sets
Wed - track session (coach) or aerobic 1 + optional Focus

Thu - speed + knee + pull: warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip / Run; A-drills never count - ORD-08) -> flying 20s -> core 2 x 2 light (ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> hurdle hops -> clean variant -> leg press or belt squat (non-axial) + row -> ipsilateral step-up (take-off - CAT-13) + pull -> slider curls -> calves 3 sets

Fri - hip + push: warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip / Run; A-drills never count - ORD-08) -> core 2 x 2 light (ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> plyo + throws -> snatch variant -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar 3-5 reps (axial day 2) + push -> single-leg RDL -> calves 3 sets
Sat - aerobic 2 (Orange / Green) or track session; Sun off
2-4 exercises per muscle trained that day (COACH-R2 SES-05); consolidate athletic work if over 12 + 2 core (COACH-R2 SES-04)
Focus (optional): hanging leg raises, inverted holds, rope / towel pull-ups, overhead lockout holds, wrist conditioning
pre_season: Mon: speed block first: squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity (fixed order, LIB-21) -> core 2 x 2 light (ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> plyo (stage held) -> clean 3 x 2-3 -> HEAVY SQUAT 3 x 3 fast intent (axial 1) + pull -> step-up -> calves
Wed: core 2 x 2 light (ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> throws + ballistic jumps -> snatch 3 x 2 -> hip thrust / belt squat (non-axial) + push -> single-leg RDL -> Nordic

profiles.template: 4 strength / power days (resistance-group sport) + track / BMX sessions

rules: plyo method stage 1 first: 'STICK THE LANDING BILATERAL' -> 'UNILATERAL' -> weighted (OBSERVED ballistics tab; CAT-10)
COD 'EASY TURN' -> 'MOD. TURN' -> 'HARD TURN' only after landing competency
single-leg strength + hip abductor work every week
athletes with an ACL history, a poor landing screen or a low training age: double the stage-1 landing block (INFERRED; replaces the v0 sex-based rule - ATH-09)
injury_prehab.extension: sports added: alpine skiing / snowboard racing and freestyle skiing (AQ37: about 15 % of young racers tore an ACL over 10 years; low leg / core strength predicted knee injury). Extra rules for snow athletes (INFERRED): hamstring strength 2 x / week (Nordic, slider curls), heavy eccentric / isometric quad work, core strength every session, reactive balance; freestyle athletes double the stage-1 landing block. Applied by landing competency and injury history, never by sex (ATH-09).

rules: spine loading (COACH-R2 SES-01/02, refines COACH-ANSWER PER-04): heavy squat and heavy deadlift once a week each, on two different days; non-axial hinge (hip thrust, back extension, reverse hyper), leg press or belt squat on the other days; axial = barbell back / front / zercher / overhead / Smith squats, barbell or trap-bar deadlifts and RDLs, good mornings
belt squat when the back was already loaded that week or is sore (EQ-11)
rotate hinge variants (hex/DB/KB) when flagged
box squats ('(D)BOX') to control depth
core = static anti-extension/anti-flexion first
injury_prehab.extension: round-2 update (supersedes the 04 'once a week' wording): heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two DIFFERENT days; non-axial hinge (hip thrust, back extension, reverse hyper), leg press or belt squat on the other days; axial = barbell back / front / zercher / overhead / Smith squats, barbell or trap-bar deadlifts and RDLs, good mornings; not axial = leg press, belt squat, hip thrust, back extension, reverse hyper, single-leg DB work, Olympic lifts, loaded jumps (COACH-R2 SES-01/02). Sports added: rowing (AQ34b: heavy squats named as an aggravating factor), track sprint cycling, shot put, road cycling (AQ32: 58 % low back pain).

injury_prehab.extension: sports added: divers (flat-hand entry - AQ14), sculling rowers, snowboarders (AQ38), pole vaulters.

rules: anti-rotation static first (Pallof holds BC46-BC49) before rotational dynamic (chops BC9/BC13/BC17, 'Woodchoppers', 'Cable Machine Oblique Rotations')

60+: no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default; offered as an option with 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means' (COACH-R2 ATH-08); landing drills (step-down and stick, no rebound) still fine; low ankle hops join the opt-in (they are on the plyometric list - COACH-R2 ATH-02); constrained machines for compounds and isolation (EQ-03)
more than 6-12 months off: the body is treated as L1 (PRG-05)
no rule depends on sex (ATH-09)
youth racers: the 10-year ACL study was in young racers (AQ37) - landing and hamstring work from the first block

derived.floor_10_note: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle': muscles listed here sit under 10 in this off-season athletic budget (athletic sets never count - VOL-10). Open question O1: does the floor apply to an athlete's non-priority muscles? Until answered the volume engine lifts the sport's PRIME muscles (resistance.priorities) to >= 10 and leaves the rest as listed (PROPOSED). v1.2: SUPERSEDED in v1.2 by derived.v1_2_group_audit: the floor of 10 is counted on focus groups (hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts) in training blocks; rear delts are not a muscle with their own floor and were removed from the legacy per-muscle lists (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01)

derived.derived_note: computed with the 04 v1 nominal reps per set (PLYO 8 contacts x (1 - landing share), JLK 20, BALL 5, THROW 10, COD 7, SPRINT 60 m, TE 4) and the generator credit map (helpers 0.25; BHD/UHD glutes 0.25 per COACH-R2 VOL-05; athletic sets credit no muscle - VOL-10). Muscle targets themselves come from the volume engine (12 / 03).

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

derived.floor_10_note: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle': muscles listed here sit under 10 in this off-season athletic budget (athletic sets never count - VOL-10). Open question O1: does the floor apply to an athlete's non-priority muscles? Until answered the volume engine lifts the sport's PRIME muscles (resistance.priorities) to >= 10 and leaves the rest as listed (PROPOSED). v1.2: SUPERSEDED in v1.2 by derived.v1_2_group_audit: the floor of 10 is counted on focus groups (hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts) in training blocks; rear delts are not a muscle with their own floor and were removed from the legacy per-muscle lists (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01)
derived.exercise_cap: 12 + 2 core for athletes with a power block (COACH-R2 SES-04)
derived.derived_note: computed with the 04 v1 nominal reps per set (PLYO 8 contacts x (1 - landing share), JLK 20, BALL 5, THROW 10, COD 7, SPRINT 60 m, TE 4) and the generator credit map (helpers 0.25; BHD/UHD glutes 0.25 per COACH-R2 VOL-05; athletic sets credit no muscle - VOL-10). Muscle targets themselves come from the volume engine (12 / 03).

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

pec-minor / thoracic mobility in the warm-up; a stiff, rounded posture plus tight pec minor is a known risk sign (AQ13)

off_season: Mon - knee + pull: warm-up -> core 2 x 2 light (COACH-R2 SES-03) -> medball (rotational throws both sides) -> ballistic jump (broad jumps / hip-in jumps) -> clean variant (hang clean -> power clean, squat pattern - COACH-R2 ATH-04) -> HEAVY SQUAT (axial day 1, COACH-R2 SES-01) + bent-over row -> contralateral split squat + pull-ups (judogi / towel pull-ups) -> gi hangs, towel farmer holds -> calves 3 sets

Tue - hip + push: real aerobic block first (Orange 20-30 min or Green 4-min match simulations, ORD-09) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo (landing sticks -> entry hops -> repeated hops, by Receive-Create stage) -> snatch variant (DB snatch -> power snatch (L2+), hinge pattern) -> non-axial hinge (hip thrust / back extension / reverse hyper) + DB bench or push-ups -> single-leg RDL -> neck isometrics 4-way (no bands - EQ-01) + rear delts -> calves
Wed - judo practice (randori)

Thu - knee + pull: core 2 x 2 -> medball -> loaded jump -> clean variant -> belt squat or leg press (non-axial) + chest-supported row -> lateral lunge (foot sweeps) -> carries / drags (sandbag carry) -> Copenhagen plank -> calves

Fri - hip + push: conditioning first (Blue 20-30 s on / 10 s off repeats) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo -> snatch variant -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) + DB press -> unilateral hinge -> biceps / triceps (elbow health) -> rear delts -> calves
Sat - randori / tournament; Sun - off; remaining aerobic sessions (colours not used yet) after practice
pre_season: Pre-competition block: 4-6 weeks at about 60 % of the off-season sets, more speed and power (COACH-R2 PER-06); 3 lifts around mat practice
Mon: core 2 x 2 -> medball (fast) -> ballistic jump -> clean variant 3-5 reps -> HEAVY SQUAT 3-5 reps (axial day 1) + bent-over row -> gi hangs, towel farmer holds -> calves
Wed: real aerobic block first -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo (stage held) -> snatch variant -> hip thrust / belt squat (non-axial) + DB press -> neck isometrics -> calves
Fri: core 2 x 2 -> medball -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) -> unilateral hinge -> pull-ups -> biceps / triceps -> calves
last 1-2 weeks before the main event = taper (volume -40-60 %, intensity kept, no new exercises - COACH-R2 PER-06)
in_season: Tournament blocks: Mon hard lift, Wed or Thu short lift, tournaments on weekends

Hard lift (>= 48 h before a match / tournament - COACH-R2 ATH-07 extended, INFERRED): core 2 x 2 -> Olympic light 2 x 3 (hang power clean or DB snatch, COACH-R2 ATH-04) -> squat OR deadlift (alternate weeks; 3-5 reps, RIR 2-3; bilateral minimal - UNI-10) + pull -> 1 unilateral -> grip -> calves
Short lift: core 2 x 2 -> unilateral + push / pull 2 sets -> neck isometrics -> rear delts
Competition day and weigh-in day: no lifting
Aerobic: 2 a week in season (COACH-ANSWER ATH-07) - an Orange flush after matches + 1 short Blue or Green
post_season: 1-2 weeks: mobility, easy Orange cardio, no athletic work (04 post_season_recovery)
then, if wanted, a maintenance phase of chosen length (a recommendation, not mandatory); when it ends the plan ends and the athlete builds the next plan in the app (COACH-R2 PER-06; COACH-R3 PER-01)
rules: power before strength; horizontal pull before vertical (ORD-01..03); hip-dominant with push, knee-dominant with pull (UNI-11)
up to 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block (COACH-R2 SES-04); muscles trained that day get 2-4 exercises (COACH-R2 SES-05)
pull sets >= push sets every week; grip and neck work 2x/week (no bands - EQ-01)
between blocks the tool may change one detail of a library exercise (hand, grip, stance, implement, range) and show it as a named variation; it never invents exercises (COACH-R2 LIB-01)

every week a step up the stairway (smaller steps early, slightly bigger after halfway, hardest weeks last); no deload or maintenance week inside a block - a block that cannot be finished is cancelled, then maintenance, then a new block (COACH-R2 PER-03/04/05, VOL-07)

no check-ins and no tracking: the plan is printed once with its planned stairway and the person or coach adjusts it ahead of time (COACH-R3 VOL-02, VOL-04); no sleep / stress / life inputs (COACH-R2 GEN-04)

Tue - overhead: core -> log clean & press (event) -> push press / axle press -> DB incline press -> rows -> triceps -> side raises + rear delts

Thu - deadlift + loading: core -> overhead backward medball throw -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / axle deadlift (axial day 2) -> stones or sandbag-to-shoulder (moderate) -> back extension -> biceps (eccentric - BICEPS_TENDON) -> calves

Sat - moving events + upper: core -> farmers carry / frame carry, sled drag or truck push (light-moderate, non-axial day) -> pull-ups -> DB bench -> grip -> event medley 60-90 s (Green) as the conditioning piece

pre_season: Contest prep 4-6 weeks: each contest event once a week at contest weight / distance (stairway in intensity), accessories cut; last 1-2 weeks taper (COACH-R2 PER-06)

post_season: 1-2 weeks: mobility, easy Orange cardio, no athletic work (04 post_season_recovery)

between blocks the tool may change one detail of a library exercise (hand, grip, stance, implement, range) and show it as a named variation; it never invents exercises (COACH-R2 LIB-01)

every week a step up the stairway (smaller steps early, slightly bigger after halfway, hardest weeks last); no deload or maintenance week inside a block - a block that cannot be finished is cancelled, then maintenance, then a new block (COACH-R2 PER-03/04/05, VOL-07)

age_50_plus.achilles_calf: ACHILLES_CALF every leg day: straight-knee and bent-knee calf raises (3 sets, VOL-17), slow lowering, progress ankle work by no more than about 10-20 % a week; a 5-min warm-up before play and before ankle work (K34c: Achilles ruptures)
age_50_plus.shoulder_elbow: rotator-cuff work (COACH-R3 ATH-02): side-lying DB external rotation, prone Y / T and KB face pulls (R2-LIB-04) 2-3 x / week; overhead pressing seated / landmine and pain-free; wrist-extensor isometrics for the paddle / racket elbow (ELBOW_LATERAL_RACKET); rotator-cuff tears are a common older-player injury (K34c)
age_50_plus.lateral: lateral shuffles, crossover steps and drop-step 'turn and run' (EASY TURN -> MOD. TURN; HARD TURN only for L2+ under 60); no fast backpedal drills (FALLS_COURT)
age_50_plus.plyo: low-impact only: RC1 landings (stick the split step / lateral stick), low-amplitude split-step pogos and lateral line hops on a forgiving surface, bilateral before single-leg; no depth jumps, hurdle hops or bounds by default at 50-59; progress only when landings are quiet and pain-free (FALLS_COURT, ACL_LANDING_CUTTING stage-1 logic); at 60+ all of it except the landing drills is opt-in with the warning (COACH-R2 ATH-08)
age_50_plus.falls_wrist: balance, reactive stepping and wrist / forearm strength every week (FALLS_COURT; wrist fractures dominate senior falls - G3)

science: 24.3 million US players in 2025 (16.8 M casual, 7.48 M core); +171.8 % in three years [G1, G2]
players 65+ were the second-largest age bracket (15.4 %) in SFIA's 2023 data [G2b]
seniors (>= 60) 2010-2019: strains / sprains 31.0 %, fractures 30.4 %; slip / trip / fall / dive 66.9 %; wrist and lower leg the most common sites; women 9.3 x more likely to fracture a wrist [G3]

racket sports: Achilles and calf problems in masters players; 'tennis leg' (medial gastrocnemius) is typical of middle-aged recreational players [G31, G32]

derived.derived_note: computed by the genpop builder: athletic doses with the 04 nominal reps per set (PLYO 8 contacts of which landing_pct are landings, JLK 20, BALL 5, THROW 10, COD 7, SPRINT 60 m, TE 4); resistance / core / calves = the 05 v1.1 athletic template for these days at 60 min, mid-block ('2-3' sets = 2.5); muscle sets with helpers 0.25 (VOL-09) and the R2-VOL-05 glute credits (BHD split hip-thrust day / deadlift day = 0.625 glutes + 0.625 hamstrings, INFERRED); FOCUS on optional days counted as arms (PROPOSED). The volume engine (12 v1.2) sets the real numbers per focus group: general factor x0.8 then the floor of 10 on groups (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01; COACH-R2 VOL-04/06); muscles listed below the floor are lifted by the engine (longer day, supersets or the optional day - R2-SES-05). Minutes = 05 time costs (60-min column), straight sets, block start ~ this value, late block longer.
derived.minutes_note: rough upper bound: 05 v1.1 time costs (60-min column) incl. set-up time, straight sets, plus this profile's athletic stations (the 05 template checks report about 63-72 min at block start for the same resistance blocks); the coach allows longer full-body days (R2-SES-05) - superset the pairs first (ORD-05); at 45 min the 05 session-length model drops stations by its cut priority (05 session_length_model.cut_priority_when_short); general clients' usual target is 45-60 min (UNI-09)

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

derived.floor_10_status_v1_2: SUPERSEDED in v1.2 by derived.v1_2_group_audit: the floor of 10 is counted on focus groups (hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts) in training blocks; rear delts are not a muscle with their own floor and were removed from the legacy per-muscle lists (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01)

training_block: Mon - S1 (jump + knee + pull; clean day): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> 2 plyo stations (split-step pogo; jump-and-stick) -> COD (lateral + forward-back) -> clean variant (KB squat clean) -> HEAVY SQUAT (axial day 1, R2-SES-01) + horizontal pull -> split squat / lunge + vertical pull -> single-leg hinge + leg curls -> side + rear delts (KB face pulls, R2-LIB-04) -> calves 2 exercises (3 sets, VOL-17)

Wed - S2 (medball + hip + push; snatch day): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> medball overhead slam + rotational throws -> 1 plyo (lateral line hops) -> snatch variant (single-arm DB snatch) -> NON-AXIAL HINGE (hip thrust / back extension / reverse hyper, R2-SES-01) + horizontal push -> single-leg hinge + vertical push -> chest fly or push-up variant + side / rear delts -> calves 2 exercises

Fri - S3 (Olympic + strength): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> COD (reactive for L2+) -> clean variant (hang clean) + wrist / grip and external rotation in the isolation block -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2, R2-SES-01) + horizontal push -> split squat / step-up + row -> leg curls + chest fly -> leg extensions + pulldown -> calves 2 exercises
Tue / Thu / Sun - matches or aerobic sessions
Sat - optional: Focus 1 / Focus 2, calves, core or an aerobic session (ORD-10)

The volume engine (12 v1.2) sets the real numbers per focus group: general factor x0.8 then the floor of 10 on groups (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01; COACH-R2 VOL-04/06); muscles listed below the floor are lifted by the engine (longer day, supersets or the optional day - R2-SES-05). training_block: Mon - A (squat + pull; clean day): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> broad jump stick + pogo (JLK) -> clean variant (KB squat clean) -> HEAVY SQUAT (axial day 1, R2-SES-01) + horizontal pull -> single-leg hinge + vertical push -> leg extensions + vertical pull -> leg curls + side / rear delts (KB face pulls, R2-LIB-04) -> calves 2 exercises (3 sets, VOL-17)

Thu - B (deadlift + push; snatch day): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> box jump or burpee broad-jump technique + ankle hops -> snatch variant (single-arm DB snatch) -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2, R2-SES-01) + horizontal push -> split squat / lunge + row -> leg curls + chest fly or push-up variant -> leg extensions + pulldown -> calves 2 exercises

Tue - hybrid 1: core 2 x 2 -> skips / pogo -> Blue run intervals (200-400 m) -> station circuit finisher 1 (sled push / pull, wall balls with the race ball <= 20 lb, burpee broad jumps) 2-4 rounds, about 8-12 min - not muscle sets (COACH-R3 ATH-03)

Sat - hybrid 2: core 2 x 2 -> Green '1 km run + 1 station' x 3-5 (race simulation) -> station circuit finisher 2 (farmers carry, sandbag lunges, SkiErg / row) 2-3 rounds - not muscle sets (COACH-R3 ATH-03)
Wed or Sun - Orange steady run or row / SkiErg 30-50 min (the second Orange)
Sun - optional: Focus / calves / core or an easy walk

derived.derived_note: computed by the genpop builder: athletic doses with the 04 nominal reps per set (PLYO 8 contacts of which landing_pct are landings, JLK 20, BALL 5, THROW 10, COD 7, SPRINT 60 m, TE 4); resistance / core / calves = the 05 v1.1 athletic template for these days at 60 min, mid-block ('2-3' sets = 2.5); muscle sets with helpers 0.25 (VOL-09) and the R2-VOL-05 glute credits (BHD split hip-thrust day / deadlift day = 0.625 glutes + 0.625 hamstrings, INFERRED); FOCUS on optional days counted as arms (PROPOSED). The volume engine (12 v1.2) sets the real numbers per focus group: general factor x0.8 then the floor of 10 on groups (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01; COACH-R2 VOL-04/06); muscles listed below the floor are lifted by the engine (longer day, supersets or the optional day - R2-SES-05). Minutes = 05 time costs (60-min column), straight sets, block start ~ this value, late block longer.
derived.minutes_note: rough upper bound: 05 v1.1 time costs (60-min column) incl. set-up time, straight sets, plus this profile's athletic stations (the 05 template checks report about 63-72 min at block start for the same resistance blocks); the coach allows longer full-body days (R2-SES-05) - superset the pairs first (ORD-05); at 45 min the 05 session-length model drops stations by its cut priority (05 session_length_model.cut_priority_when_short); general clients' usual target is 45-60 min (UNI-09)

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

derived.floor_10_status_v1_2: SUPERSEDED in v1.2 by derived.v1_2_group_audit: the floor of 10 is counted on focus groups (hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts) in training blocks; rear delts are not a muscle with their own floor and were removed from the legacy per-muscle lists (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01)

training_block: Mon - S1 (jump + knee + pull; clean day): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> step-up jump + ankle hops -> footwork (EASY TURN) -> clean variant (KB squat clean) -> HEAVY SQUAT (axial day 1, R2-SES-01) + horizontal pull -> split squat / lunge + vertical pull -> single-leg hinge + leg curls -> side + rear delts (KB face pulls, R2-LIB-04) -> calves 2 exercises (3 sets, VOL-17)

Wed - S2 (medball + hip + push; snatch day): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> medball slam -> box jump stick -> snatch variant + farmers carry -> NON-AXIAL HINGE (hip thrust / back extension / reverse hyper, R2-SES-01) + horizontal push -> single-leg hinge + vertical push -> chest fly or push-up variant + side / rear delts -> calves 2 exercises

Fri - S3 (Olympic + strength): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> hex-bar jump -> step-downs (slow) in the knee block + suitcase carry -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2, R2-SES-01) + horizontal push -> split squat / step-up + row -> leg curls + chest fly -> leg extensions + pulldown -> calves 2 exercises
Sat or Sun - the hike or ruck (Orange)
Tue or Thu - incline treadmill / stair intervals (Green)
Sat - optional: Focus 1 / Focus 2, calves, core or an aerobic session (ORD-10)

up to 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block; a superset of two small isolations counts as one (R2-SES-04)

the heavy deadlift day is not the day before a long ruck

derived.derived_note: computed by the genpop builder: athletic doses with the 04 nominal reps per set (PLYO 8 contacts of which landing_pct are landings, JLK 20, BALL 5, THROW 10, COD 7, SPRINT 60 m, TE 4); resistance / core / calves = the 05 v1.1 athletic template for these days at 60 min, mid-block ('2-3' sets = 2.5); muscle sets with helpers 0.25 (VOL-09) and the R2-VOL-05 glute credits (BHD split hip-thrust day / deadlift day = 0.625 glutes + 0.625 hamstrings, INFERRED); FOCUS on optional days counted as arms (PROPOSED). The volume engine (12 v1.2) sets the real numbers per focus group: general factor x0.8 then the floor of 10 on groups (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01; COACH-R2 VOL-04/06); muscles listed below the floor are lifted by the engine (longer day, supersets or the optional day - R2-SES-05). Minutes = 05 time costs (60-min column), straight sets, block start ~ this value, late block longer.
derived.minutes_note: rough upper bound: 05 v1.1 time costs (60-min column) incl. set-up time, straight sets, plus this profile's athletic stations (the 05 template checks report about 63-72 min at block start for the same resistance blocks); the coach allows longer full-body days (R2-SES-05) - superset the pairs first (ORD-05); at 45 min the 05 session-length model drops stations by its cut priority (05 session_length_model.cut_priority_when_short); general clients' usual target is 45-60 min (UNI-09)

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

derived.floor_10_status_v1_2: SUPERSEDED in v1.2 by derived.v1_2_group_audit: the floor of 10 is counted on focus groups (hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts) in training blocks; rear delts are not a muscle with their own floor and were removed from the legacy per-muscle lists (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01)

emphasis.scale: 0 none - 1 low - 2 moderate - 3 high, from the 04 tier of the weekly dose (plyometric contacts, throws, cuts, sprint metres); a jump score of 1 with no fast-reactive contacts = low-amplitude / ballistic jumps only

Thu - B (deadlift + push; snatch day): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> squat jump stick + medball slam -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2, R2-SES-01) + horizontal push -> split squat / lunge + row -> leg curls + chest fly or push-up variant -> leg extensions + pulldown -> calves 2 exercises

Sat - ride 2 (Orange long ride)
Thu or Sun - ride 3 (Green climbs)

derived.derived_note: computed by the genpop builder: athletic doses with the 04 nominal reps per set (PLYO 8 contacts of which landing_pct are landings, JLK 20, BALL 5, THROW 10, COD 7, SPRINT 60 m, TE 4); resistance / core / calves = the 05 v1.1 athletic template for these days at 60 min, mid-block ('2-3' sets = 2.5); muscle sets with helpers 0.25 (VOL-09) and the R2-VOL-05 glute credits (BHD split hip-thrust day / deadlift day = 0.625 glutes + 0.625 hamstrings, INFERRED); FOCUS on optional days counted as arms (PROPOSED). The volume engine (12 v1.2) sets the real numbers per focus group: general factor x0.8 then the floor of 10 on groups (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01; COACH-R2 VOL-04/06); muscles listed below the floor are lifted by the engine (longer day, supersets or the optional day - R2-SES-05). Minutes = 05 time costs (60-min column), straight sets, block start ~ this value, late block longer.
derived.minutes_note: rough upper bound: 05 v1.1 time costs (60-min column) incl. set-up time, straight sets, plus this profile's athletic stations (the 05 template checks report about 63-72 min at block start for the same resistance blocks); the coach allows longer full-body days (R2-SES-05) - superset the pairs first (ORD-05); at 45 min the 05 session-length model drops stations by its cut priority (05 session_length_model.cut_priority_when_short); general clients' usual target is 45-60 min (UNI-09)

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

derived.floor_10_status_v1_2: SUPERSEDED in v1.2 by derived.v1_2_group_audit: the floor of 10 is counted on focus groups (hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts) in training blocks; rear delts are not a muscle with their own floor and were removed from the legacy per-muscle lists (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01)

The volume engine (12 v1.2) sets the real numbers per focus group: general factor x0.8 then the floor of 10 on groups (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01; COACH-R2 VOL-04/06); muscles listed below the floor are lifted by the engine (longer day, supersets or the optional day - R2-SES-05).
