derived.derived_note: computed by the genpop builder: athletic doses with the 04 nominal reps per set (PLYO 8 contacts of which landing_pct are landings, JLK 20, BALL 5, THROW 10, COD 7, SPRINT 60 m, TE 4); resistance / core / calves = the 05 v1.1 athletic template for these days at 60 min, mid-block ('2-3' sets = 2.5); muscle sets with helpers 0.25 (VOL-09) and the R2-VOL-05 glute credits (BHD split hip-thrust day / deadlift day = 0.625 glutes + 0.625 hamstrings, INFERRED); FOCUS on optional days counted as arms (PROPOSED). The volume engine (12 v1.2) sets the real numbers per focus group: general factor x0.8 then the floor of 10 on groups (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01; COACH-R2 VOL-04/06); muscles listed below the floor are lifted by the engine (longer day, supersets or the optional day - R2-SES-05). Minutes = 05 time costs (60-min column), straight sets, block start ~ this value, late block longer.
derived.minutes_note: rough upper bound: 05 v1.1 time costs (60-min column) incl. set-up time, straight sets, plus this profile's athletic stations (the 05 template checks report about 63-72 min at block start for the same resistance blocks); the coach allows longer full-body days (R2-SES-05) - superset the pairs first (ORD-05); at 45 min the 05 session-length model drops stations by its cut priority (05 session_length_model.cut_priority_when_short); general clients' usual target is 45-60 min (UNI-09)

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)
v1_1_audit.superseded_by: derived.v1_2_group_audit (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01: the floor counts on groups; rear delts belong to the shoulders group)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

derived.floor_10_status_v1_2: SUPERSEDED in v1.2 by derived.v1_2_group_audit: the floor of 10 is counted on focus groups (hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts) in training blocks; rear delts are not a muscle with their own floor and were removed from the legacy per-muscle lists (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01)

The volume engine (12 v1.2) sets the real numbers per focus group: general factor x0.8 then the floor of 10 on groups (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01; COACH-R2 VOL-04/06); muscles listed below the floor are lifted by the engine (longer day, supersets or the optional day - R2-SES-05). Minutes = 05 time costs (60-min column), straight sets, block start ~ this value, late block longer.

v1_1_audit.credits: category-level credits: main mover 1.0, helpers 0.25; BHD / UHD credit glutes 0.25 (COACH-R2 VOL-05: deadlifts / RDLs a quarter set) - hip thrusts / bridges (1.0) and glute isolation are credited per exercise by the engine, so glutes here are a lower bound; KB swings credit nothing (COACH-R2 VOL-05); athletic work credits no muscle (VOL-10)
v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

Fri - S3 (fast machine power + strength; Olympic lifts only if switched on): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> reactive stepping -> fast cable row or hip thrust machine -> sit-to-stand / step-ups -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2, R2-SES-01) + horizontal push -> split squat / step-up + row -> leg curls + chest fly -> leg extensions + pulldown -> calves 2 exercises

The volume engine (12 v1.2) sets the real numbers per focus group: general factor x0.8 then the floor of 10 on groups (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01; COACH-R2 VOL-04/06); muscles listed below the floor are lifted by the engine (longer day, supersets or the optional day - R2-SES-05). v1_1_audit.floor_rule: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle' - the volume engine raises targets; for athletes the PROPOSED reading is that the floor applies to the muscles the plan trains for size / strength in the off-season (open question)

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

profiles.rationale: Bouldering and rope-climbing gyms are a fast-growing way adults stay athletic. The wall already gives a lot of pulling and finger load, so the gym plan balances it: antagonist pushing and shoulder external rotation, wrist-extensor and grip balance, legs and hips for high steps, trunk tension, and landing practice for bouldering falls. Finger-specific training (hangboard) is for L2+ only and follows FINGER_PULLEY. Contact class 5 (sustained contact, 25 % plyometric).

v1_2_group_audit.note: v1.2 group audit (COACH-R3 SES-01, VOL-01): sets counted on FOCUS GROUPS - hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor); each category credits a group once at its highest credit (main mover 1.0, helper groups 0.25), so an RDL is one hip set, not 1.25; athletic work credits nothing (VOL-10); the floor of 10 applies to the groups a TRAINING block trains (maintenance, pre- and in-season are lower by design); time-short plans train fewer groups directly and leave arms, calves and shoulder isolation to compound credit (COACH-R3 SES-02); descriptive budget check only - 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 owns the engine math

Tue - Blue: hill repeats or run intervals

Thu - B (deadlift + push; snatch day): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> broad jump stick + single-leg hops (RC stage) -> snatch variant (single-arm DB snatch) -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2, R2-SES-01) + push-up -> lunge + rope / towel row -> leg curls + farmers / bucket carry -> calves 2 exercises

v1_1_sports.topic: Floor of 10 weekly sets per muscle vs athlete budgets
v1_1_sports.detail: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle.' The 04 athlete budgets reused here give field athletes far fewer direct upper-body sets (e.g. soccer chest about 2-4). Proposed reading: the floor applies to muscles the athlete's plan trains for size / strength in the off-season; pre-season (about 60 %) and in-season blocks are maintenance phases and may sit below 10. Needs the coach's yes.
v1_1_sports.status: OPEN - flag to the volume engine owner
v1_1_sports.status_v1_2: PARTLY ANSWERED by COACH-R3 VOL-01 / SES-01: the floor of 10 is counted on groups in training blocks; maintenance, pre- and in-season stay lower; 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.4 sets the athlete group floors (chest, back, shoulders to 10; arms from compound credit)

v1_1_sports.topic: 2-4 exercises per muscle on full-body days vs the 12 + 2 cap
v1_1_sports.detail: COACH-R2 SES-05 (2-4 exercises per muscle on full-body days, never 1) and COACH-R2 SES-04 (field athletes up to 12 exercises + 2 core) collide on athletic full-body days that already hold 4-6 athletic exercises. Proposed: 2-4 exercises for each muscle TRAINED that day (knee + pull day / hip + push day pairing), not for every muscle; athletic exercises do not count toward the cap's resistance part.
v1_1_sports.status_v1_2: ANSWERED by COACH-R3 SES-01: 2-4 exercises for each group trained that day (knee + pull day, hip + push day) inside 12 + 2 core; cross pattern (default) leaves 2 jump / throw stations + 1 Olympic lift; the same-pattern template for size-focused / high-level athletes

v1_1_sports.topic: Weightlifting and the two-axial-days rule
v1_1_sports.detail: COACH-R2 SES-01/02: heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days, other days non-axial; the approved exception is a light technique squat or deadlift for powerlifters. Weightlifters traditionally squat heavy 2-3x a week. Proposed: heavy back squat day + heavy pull (clean deadlift / pull) day; the front squat stays light-moderate (same exception as powerlifters). Needs the coach.

v1_1_sports.topic: Fight camps vs COACH-R2 PER-06 and the OBSERVED boxing build-up
v1_1_sports.detail: The OBSERVED boxing tab builds weeks 3-8 (+41 % component sets) with a week-7 mini-deload. COACH-R2 VOL-07 removes deloads inside a block, and COACH-R2 PER-06 makes the pre-season block about 60 % of off-season sets with more speed and power + a 1-2-week taper. Resolution used: off-camp = off-season blocks (the 8-week build is the coach's example of one), camp = the 4-6-week pre-season block at about 60 %, then the 1-2-week taper to the fight; the week-7 mini-deload is retired as a default (OBSERVED example only).

v1_1_sports.topic: Aerobic sessions in race-prep blocks (HYROX, OCR)
v1_1_sports.detail: COACH-R2 ATH-06 approved 'pre-season 2' for athletes. HYROX is about 60 % running (K18) and OCR is mostly trail running, so cutting to 2 aerobic sessions before a race would remove the main work. Proposed: HYROX / OCR keep 4 in the race-specific block (3 between races); gym sets still drop to about 60 % (COACH-R2 PER-06).
v1_1_sports.status_v1_2: ANSWERED for HYROX by COACH-R3 ATH-03 (4 cardio sessions); OCR by analogy (PROPOSED)

v1_1_sports.topic: 60+ competitive athletes (senior pickleball, masters lifters, masters grapplers)
v1_1_sports.detail: COACH-R2 ATH-08: 60+ get no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default, with an opt-in and the warning 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means.' Our round-2 proposal also said landing drills and low ankle hops stay OK; the coach's words say no plyos by default. Profiles use the stricter reading (none by default; balance, step-ups and fast-intent resistance instead). For a masters weightlifter the Olympic lifts are the sport - they opt in with the warning. Confirm both.
v1_1_sports.status_v1_2: ANSWERED by COACH-R3 ATH-02 (60+ defaults; Olympic lifts, other jumps and depth jumps switchable with the warning - a masters weightlifter switches the lifts on)

v1_1_sports.detail: COACH-R2 GEN-06: '% only ... unless you're a competitive Olympic lifter. That becomes a nuance, and now the program needs to change to Olympic weightlifting programming.' The weightlifting profile is a scaffold (4-day snatch / clean & jerk week, % of each lift's 1RM, 1-3 reps on the competition lifts). The coach has not written one - needs his template or approval.

v1_1_sports.topic: Where cleans and snatches sit in the week
v1_1_sports.detail: COACH-R2 ATH-04: cleans read as squat-pattern, snatches as hinge-pattern, up to 4 exposures a week. team.json places cleans on knee days and snatches on hip days; the coach's own CrossFit split (OBSERVED) puts snatches on both lower days (Mon knee dom, Thu hip dom) and cleans on the upper days. Both are used here (team convention for athletes, OBSERVED split for CrossFit). Is the pattern a day-placement rule or only a balance rule?

v1_1_sports.topic: CrossFit class / bootcamp muscle volume
v1_1_sports.detail: In the OBSERVED class split only the strength / power slots are sets (about 15 a week); the WOD carries most of the work but is conditioning (VOL-10 logic), so every muscle sits below 10. Options: count WOD resistance movements at a fraction, or add a RESISTANCE slot (the FULL / HALF TIME tables have 'RESISTANCE LVL 1 = 2 SETS x 10'). This matters for the 'CrossFit-style bootcamp' sample plan the coach will grade (COACH-R2 GEN-07).

v1_1_sports.topic: Physique contest prep and peak week
v1_1_sports.detail: Proposed: prep = 1-2 full blocks (no deload inside, COACH-R2 VOL-07) at about 90 % of off-season sets with longer cardio and daily walks; peak week about -45 %, no new exercises. The tool gives no nutrition, water or posing-schedule advice (COACH-R2 GEN-04: workouts only). Division priority deltas (bikini glutes / shoulders, men's physique V-taper, wellness lower body) are PROPOSED.

Shoulder pain and disability across the lifespan of competitive swimmers: 19.4% of masters swimmers (23-77 y), more at 40-60; risk = swim exposure, prior trauma, instability, less cross-training; pec-minor tightness and low core endurance in symptomatic swimmers

Competitive divers (systematic review 2024): shoulder, lumbar spine, trunk and wrist/hand most injured; low back pain up to 89% lifetime; spondylolysis from repetitive hyperextension; more injuries on entries, back / reverse dives and platform

Horizontal jumps (championship biomechanics): long-jump take-off contact 0.12-0.14 s; triple jump hop 0.12-0.14, step 0.13-0.15, jump 0.14-0.16 s

Javelin injuries (10-year overview): shoulder ~30% of injuries; medial UCL sprain ('javelin thrower's elbow') the most common injury; also low back and knee
Preventing shoulder injuries in throwers and pole vaulters (Aspetar Sports Medicine Journal, athletics issue)

Elite sprint cyclists: back-squat maximal force and power-clean maximal power the strongest predictors of on-bike force and power

Judo time-motion by championship phase, 53,403 actions (J Hum Kinet 2018)
